linked_prs.title: Add Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Approval System for Sensitive Operations
linked_prs.body:
## Overview

Implements Phase 1 of Human-in-the-Loop capabilities for AgenticFleet, addressing issue #OPT-03. This adds critical safety controls by requiring human approval before executing sensitive operations like code execution, providing transparency, compliance, and user trust.

## Problem

AgenticFleet agents currently execute operations autonomously without human oversight, creating risks:
- No mechanism to review code before execution
- Cannot prevent potentially harmful operations (file deletion, external API calls, etc.)
- No way to modify agent-generated code before running it
- Missing audit trail for compliance requirements
- Users have no control over what agents do with their data

## Solution

Implemented a flexible approval system that intercepts sensitive operations and presents them to users for review:

**Core Architecture:**
- `ApprovalHandler` abstract interface for custom implementations
- `CLIApprovalHandler` provides terminal-based approval UI
- `ApprovalRequest` and `ApprovalResponse` Pydantic models for type safety
- Tool wrapper system that checks for approval handler before execution

**User Experience:**
When the coder agent wants to execute code, users see:

```
============================================================
⚠️  APPROVAL REQUIRED
============================================================
Agent:       coder
Operation:   code_execution
Description: Execute Python code
Code:        print('Hello, World!')
============================================================

Approve? (yes/no/edit):
```

Users can:
- **Approve** (`yes`) - Execute code as shown
- **Reject** (`no`) - Block execution with optional reason
- **Modify** (`edit`) - Edit code before execution

## Configuration

HITL is enabled by default in `workflow.yaml`:

```yaml
human_in_the_loop:
  enabled: true
  approval_timeout_seconds: 300  # 5 minutes
  auto_reject_on_timeout: false  # Safe default
  require_approval_for:
    - code_execution
    - file_operations
    - external_api_calls
    - sensitive_data_access
  trusted_operations:
    - web_search
    - data_analysis
```

## Key Features

✅ **Interactive Approval** - Clear CLI prompts with operation details  
✅ **Code Modification** - Edit operations before execution  
✅ **Timeout Handling** - Configurable timeout with safe defaults  
✅ **Approval History** - In-memory tracking for audit trails  
✅ **Operation Control** - Configure which operations require approval  
✅ **Zero Breaking Changes** - Fully backward compatible  
✅ **Safe Defaults** - HITL enabled, no auto-reject on timeout  

## Implementation Details

**Files Added:**
- `src/agenticfleet/core/approval.py` - Core interfaces and models
- `src/agenticfleet/core/cli_approval.py` - CLI approval handler
- `src/agenticfleet/core/approved_tools.py` - Tool wrapper system
- `tests/test_hitl.py` - Comprehensive test suite
- `docs/guides/human-in-the-loop.md` - Complete user guide

**Integration Points:**
- Modified `code_interpreter.py` to check for approval handler
- Updated `workflow_builder.py` to initialize handler from config
- Enhanced `repl.py` to display HITL status on startup
- Added HITL configuration section to `workflow.yaml`

## Testing

All tests pass successfully:
- ✅ Approval request creation and handling
- ✅ Approve/reject/modify decision flows
- ✅ Code execution integration
- ✅ Timeout behavior
- ✅ History tracking
- ✅ CLI integration

Includes both automated tests (`test_hitl.py`) and manual test runner (`test_hitl_manual.py`) plus interactive demo script (`demo_hitl.py`).

## Security Benefits

- 🛡️ Prevents harmful code execution by requiring review
- 🛡️ Blocks dangerous operations before they execute
- 🛡️ Allows modification of risky operations
- 🛡️ Provides audit trail for compliance
- 🛡️ Configurable operation types for fine-grained control

## Documentation

Comprehensive documentation includes:
- **User Guide** - Quick start, configuration, use cases, troubleshooting
- **Implementation Summary** - Architecture details, testing results
- **Visual Documentation** - Flow diagrams, CLI examples
- **API Reference** - Creating custom approval handlers

## Production Ready

✅ Zero breaking changes - Fully backward compatible  
✅ No new dependencies - Uses existing packages  
✅ Safe by default - HITL enabled in configuration  
✅ Minimal overhead - Efficient when disabled  
✅ Well tested - 100% test coverage  
✅ Fully documented - User guide + API docs  

## Usage Example

```bash
$ python -m agenticfleet

✓ Human-in-the-Loop enabled (timeout: 300s)
  Operations requiring approval: code_execution, ...

🎯 Your task: Calculate fibonacci numbers

⚠️  APPROVAL REQUIRED
Code: def fib(n): ...

Approve? (yes/no/edit): yes
[Approved] Executing...
0 1 1 2 3 5 8 13...
```

## Future Enhancements

Phase 2 and 3 features (out of scope for this PR):
- Persistent approval history/audit logs
- Web UI for approvals
- Approval queuing and delegation
- Mobile notifications
- Batch approval features
- Analytics dashboard

Closes #OPT-03

title: [Gen-AI] Sync indexing tools breaks as PGVector is async
body:
I noticed that PGVector is instanced in async mode here : https://github.com/theopenconversationkit/tock/blob/master/gen-ai/orchestrator-server/src/main/python/server/src/gen_ai_orchestrator/services/langchain/factories/vector_stores/pgvector_factory.py#L53 

Which lead to the following error when using index_documents.py (toolings) this is now sync (not async) : 
```bash
INFO:index_documents:i=0, splitted_docs=6
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tock/gen-ai/orchestrator-server/src/main/python/tock-llm-indexing-tools/index_documents.py", line 426, in <module>
    details = index_documents()
  File "tock/gen-ai/orchestrator-server/src/main/python/tock-llm-indexing-tools/index_documents.py", line 183, in index_documents
    embedding_and_indexing(splitted_docs, vector_store)
  File "tock/gen-ai/orchestrator-server/src/main/python/tock-llm-indexing-tools/index_documents.py", line 273, in embedding_and_indexing
    vector_store.add_documents(documents=splitted_docs[i: i + embedding_bulk_size], bulk_size=embedding_bulk_size)
  File "tock/gen-ai/orchestrator-server/src/main/python/tock-llm-indexing-tools/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/langchain_core/vectorstores/base.py", line 287, in add_documents
    return self.add_texts(texts, metadatas, **kwargs)
  File "tock/gen-ai/orchestrator-server/src/main/python/tock-llm-indexing-tools/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/langchain_postgres/vectorstores.py", line 883, in add_texts
    assert not self._async_engine, "This method must be called without async_mode"
AssertionError: This method must be called without async_mode
```

One way to solve it would be to let the use choose the method used sync / async optionally in the settings, enforce it as async when the factory is used in the indexing tools maybe.

### Bug Description

```
undefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefinedundefined

Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')

## Summary

- Fixes issue #181
- Session context is now injected dynamically via `systemPrompt.append` instead of modifying CLAUDE.md on disk
- Eliminates race conditions, file system pollution, and persistence issues

## Problem

Previously, the Agor session context was being injected by modifying CLAUDE.md on disk. This approach caused:
- Race conditions with concurrent sessions
- File system pollution (temporary session data persisted on disk)
- Difficulty maintaining clean working directories

## Solution

The session context is now generated dynamically and passed via the `systemPrompt.append` field in the Claude Code SDK query options. This is a cleaner, more reliable approach that:
- Prevents file system modifications
- Eliminates race conditions
- Keeps session context ephemeral (exists only during the session)

- Removed `appendSessionContextToCLAUDEmd` call from `setupQuery`
- Added `systemPrompt.append` field with `generateSessionContext(sessionId)` in query options
- Updated AGENTS.md to reflect current session ID

title: Issue with Google Gemini Chat Model Node - Gemma Models No Longer Support Images (Regression)

### Bug Description

The `Google Gemini Chat Model` node no longer supports image inputs when using Gemma models. Executing the node with an image results in an error stating that Gemma models do not support images.

This is a regression from previous versions where this functionality worked correctly. This change breaks critical production workflows that rely on Gemma models for image processing.

Notably, the new standalone `Gemini` node *does* handle images correctly with the same models. The issue seems to be specific to the `Google Gemini Chat Model` node and its integration (possibly via LangChain), as the official Google Gemini API supports multimodal inputs for these models.

    *   Under **Model**, select `Chat Model`.
    *   For the **Chat Model**, choose `Google Gemini Chat Model`.
    *   Configure the node with your credentials and select a big gemma model (e.g., `models/gemma-3-27b-it`).
    *   Under **Options**, enable the **Pass In Binary Data** toggle.
5.  Save and activate the workflow.
6.  Open the chat interface provided by the `Chat Trigger`.

title: LLaMA utf-8 problems
body:
Running llama.cpp directly seems to always return valid UTF8, but the `llm-chain-llama` gets invalid utf8 and panics on `unwrap`ing `CStr` to `String` about 90% of the time I talk in Chinese with it. I replaced [that](https://github.com/sobelio/llm-chain/blob/3cff4450b89c6922b132a387260331f9d6d305fb/crates/llm-chain-llama/src/context.rs#L255C16-L255C16) with the `from_utf8_lossy` which replaces invalid bytes with a question mark symbol. I noticed that all the question marks come in pairs of 3 which is how many bytes most Chinese characters are encoded as.

For example:
`���小平在经���体制改���方面���的取得了���大成功，他������加工业化和开放政���，这些policy有助于打造现代中国。在1978年，���小平实行的改���包���：���出自主经���道路、建立特色社会主义市场经���制度和���收西方科技等。这些变化������地改变了中国经���的形状，导���全球���的经������长和实现了人民日常生活水平上的提高。`

I suspect it is because of it taking many `CStr`s from the FFI, then each converts them individually with `StreamSegment` rather than all together, and sometimes the segments end inside the bytes of a character, so some of the character is in the previous segment, some of it in the next. Then when it converts it to a string the word that got split into two segments ends up becoming invalid in each segment, but valid if the bytes from the `CStr`s were all combined. This doesn't affect ASCII since all letters are only 1 byte so they are always valid no matter which byte the string is cut.

I can think of two ways to fix this. Have `Output` do `Vec<u8>` instead of `String` and then have the user handle gluing the bytes together, or have the `Executor` have some state that will store the last few bytes if they are invalid and then prepend them to the front of the next chunk of bytes. The second way is a little more complicated but would save the users more hassle and won't mess with the rest of the library.

linked_prs.title: LLaMA handling unicode
linked_prs.body:
Fixes
https://github.com/sobelio/llm-chain/issues/187


[Handle this specific utf8 error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/str/struct.Utf8Error.html#method.error_len)
`None: the end of the input was reached unexpectedly. self.valid_up_to() is 1 to 3 bytes from the end of the input. If a byte stream (such as a file or a network socket) is being decoded incrementally, this could be a valid char whose UTF-8 byte sequence is spanning multiple chunks.`

The LLaMA `Executor` cuts off at arbitrary bytes which works for ascii but not multi-byte utf8. Add a buffer that will keep the extra bytes until the next chunk comes in where it will prepend it and add the missing bytes back onto it. It will also replace actually broken utf-8 (not just cut off) with the `std::char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER` instead of panicking the thread.

linked_prs.body:
Implementation of #194 . The key-binding is Control+Space, which doesn't conflict on zsh nor bash.

I decided most commands *sgpt* spits out are good enough to execute directly without supervision. This makes the natural language interface really make it feel like an English shell. However, there are two hacks when executing a natural language command directly that should be discussed:
1. The way command_not_found_handler decides if its English is whether the first word is upper cased and there are at least 6 words in the sentence. I figured this because natural language is more verbose than bash, so an arbitrary length threshold is a good heuristic.
2. The way _sgpt_is_destructive_command checks if the command is destructive is manually check if its in the list (rm mv dd chmod sed git mkfs mkswap). There are of course many more destructive commands, and to be safe the script should be checking a wider range of them.

I also added a .gitignore file with GitHub's Python template because __pycache__ files kept being recognized by git.

If you agree with this interface, the next thing to do is update pyproject.toml to prompt the user to update their shell rc to source this shell script, and update documentation for the --describe-shell flag.

title: MCP Error -32603: 422 Invalid request - 'sha' wasn't supplied when updating file
body:
## Description
When trying to update a file using the create_or_update_file tool, I'm encountering an error where the SHA parameter isn't being supplied, resulting in a 422 Invalid request from the GitHub API.

## Error Message
```
Failed to call tool create_or_update_file: Error: MCP error -32603: failed to https://api.github.com/repos/evanmcgillivray/Budget/contents/src/components
422 Invalid request. "sha" wasn't supplied. []
```

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Using the MCP server with an AI assistant
2. Attempting to update a file in a repository
3. The MCP server fails to include the required SHA parameter in the request

## Expected Behavior
The MCP server should properly include the SHA parameter when updating files, as required by the GitHub API.

## Additional Information
- GitHub requires the SHA parameter when updating a file to ensure you're updating the correct version
- This appears to be happening specifically when trying to update a file via the create_or_update_file function

linked_prs.title: Fix: Specify sha is required for file update
linked_prs.body:
<!--
    Thank you for contributing to GitHub MCP Server!
    Please reference an existing issue: `Closes #NUMBER`

    Screenshots or videos of changed behavior is incredibly helpful and always appreciated.
    Consider addressing the following:
    - Tradeoffs: List tradeoffs you made to take on or pay down tech debt.
    - Alternatives: Describe alternative approaches you considered and why you discarded them.
-->

Closes: #191

## The problem

When the LLM sends an `update_file` request, it doesn't include the `sha` of the file being replaced, leading to the error:
```
Failed to call tool create_or_update_file: Error: MCP error -32603: failed to https://api.github.com/repos/evanmcgillivray/Budget/contents/src/components
422 Invalid request. "sha" wasn't supplied. []
```

This happens because `sha` is an optional field since the same tool is used for both `create` and `update` file operations.

## The solution

I did some local testing and the issue seems to be fixed if we specify in the tool description that `sha` is required when updating a file.

However, a more robust solution might be to split the tool into 2 separate tools and and make a new `update_file` tool that has a required `sha` property. 

I wasn't sure which approach would be preferred, so I've decided to put forward the simplest solution that works to hear your feedback.

Yes.  
This is an agent issue because it involves a tool invocation failure within an LLM-based agent system (the create_or_update_file tool), specifically a misused or missing parameter required for the tool to function correctly, which matches the "Misuse tool interfaces" sub-category.

linked_prs.body:
## Summary

This PR provides a comprehensive fix for Ollama LLM integration issues that were preventing proper responses and causing configuration validation errors. The changes ensure that both the regular CLI (`lf run`) and the internal development chat (`lf dev`) work correctly out of the box.

**Fixes #193** - Dev chat fails with 422 validation errors

To test, please build the CLI and use ./lf at project root to test lf dev :)

```bash
# From the repository root
cd cli
go build -o ../lf .
cd ..
```

## Problems Solved

### 1. Empty Response Issue ("No response received") 🔧
**Problem:** Users were getting empty responses when using `lf run` commands  
**Root Cause:** The instructor library was receiving "404 page not found" errors from Ollama because the base URL was incorrect  
**Solution:** Updated base_url configuration to use Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `/v1`

### 2. Response Reflection Issue 🔄
**Problem:** The LLM was echoing back user questions instead of providing answers  
**Root Cause:** Inadequate system prompt allowing the model to repeat inputs  
**Solution:** Implemented comprehensive system prompt with explicit anti-reflection rules and JSON formatting instructions

### 3. New Project Initialization Failures 🚫
**Problem:** Projects created with `lf init` would fail with "None is not of type 'string'" validation errors  
**Root Cause:** Missing `instructor_mode` parameter in configuration templates  
**Solution:** Added `instructor_mode: md_json` as default in all templates

### 4. Dev Chat 422 Validation Errors (Issue #193) ✅
**Problem:** `lf dev` command failed with "Input should be 'system', 'user' or 'assistant'" errors  
**Root Cause:** CLI was sending messages with role "client" which isn't valid for the API  
**Solution:** Added filtering to remove "client" and "error" role messages before sending to server

### 5. Instructor Mode Enum Handling 🔧
**Problem:** Server crashed with "InstructorMode object has no attribute 'upper'" after datamodel regeneration  
**Root Cause:** Code expected string but got enum object after schema regeneration  
**Solution:** Updated orchestrator to properly handle instructor_mode as enum with null checking

### 6. Missing Dataset Models 📊
**Problem:** DatasetFile and DatasetWithFileDetails models disappeared after schema regeneration  
**Root Cause:** These were manually added to datamodel.py but not in schema  
**Solution:** Added these models to schema.yaml so they persist through regeneration

## Detailed Changes

### Configuration Templates (`config/templates/`)
- ✅ Added `instructor_mode: md_json` to runtime configuration
- ✅ Updated `base_url` to include `/v1` suffix: `http://localhost:11434/v1`
- ✅ Added comprehensive system prompt with anti-reflection rules
- ✅ Applied changes to both `default.yaml` and `advanced.yaml` templates

### Schema Updates (`config/schema.yaml`, `rag/schema.yaml`)
- ✅ Made optional fields accept null values (`api_key`, `base_url`, `instructor_mode`)
- ✅ Added enum validation for `instructor_mode`: `[tools, json, md_json, null]`
- ✅ Added `DatasetFile` and `DatasetWithFileDetails` models to schema
- ✅ Updated RAG schema to allow null for optional fields

### CLI Fixes (`cli/cmd/chat_client.go`)
- ✅ Filter out "client" and "error" role messages before sending to API
- ✅ Prevents 422 validation errors in `lf dev` command

### Project Seed Configuration (`server/seeds/project_seed/llamafarm.yaml`)
- ✅ Updated to use correct instructor_mode and base_url
- ✅ Simplified system prompt to prevent confusion
- ✅ Set api_key to null for Ollama

### Server Improvements (`server/agents/project_chat_orchestrator.py`)
- ✅ Fixed instructor_mode enum handling with proper null checking
- ✅ Respects configured mode instead of forcing JSON mode
- ✅ Defaults to MD_JSON for Ollama (most compatible)
- ✅ Improved error handling and logging

### Datamodel Generation (`config/datamodel.py`)
- ✅ Regenerated with all required models from schema
- ✅ Includes DatasetFile and DatasetWithFileDetails
- ✅ Proper InstructorMode enum with null handling

## Technical Background

### Instructor Modes
The instructor library provides structured output through different modes:
- **TOOLS**: Function calling (not supported by Ollama)
- **JSON**: Direct JSON output (less reliable)
- **MD_JSON**: Markdown-wrapped JSON (best for Ollama)

We standardized on `MD_JSON` for Ollama as it provides the best compatibility.

### Ollama OpenAI Compatibility
Ollama provides an OpenAI-compatible API at `/v1`. This must be explicitly specified in the base_url for the instructor library to work correctly.

## Testing Performed

- ✅ Verified `lf init` creates working projects without manual fixes
- ✅ Tested `lf run` returns proper responses (not reflections)
- ✅ Confirmed `lf dev` no longer throws 422 validation errors
- ✅ Validated RAG functionality works correctly
- ✅ Tested with multiple Ollama models (llama3.1:8b, qwen3:8b)
- ✅ Verified schema regeneration preserves all required models
- ✅ Confirmed instructor mode respects configuration

## Impact

This PR ensures:

- 🎯 No manual configuration fixes required
- 🎯 Both regular CLI and dev chat work out of the box
- 🎯 Proper LLM responses instead of empty or reflected content
- 🎯 Schema regeneration doesn't break the server
- 🎯 Consistent behavior across all Ollama models

## Breaking Changes

None - all changes are backward compatible.

title: EventActions does not capture all the action when there are multiple function calls in an Event
body:
**Describe the bug**
EventActions does not capture all the action when there are multiple function calls in an Event. 

For example, if an Event generated from LLM contains two `functionCall`
```
content:
  parts:
    0:
      functionCall:
        id: "adk-645f8032-712b-41a7-8e27-64c49f977522"
      args:
        query: "arg1"
      name: "state_update_tool1"
    1:
      functionCall:
        id: "adk-645f8032-712b-41a7-8e27-64c49f977522"
      args:
        query: "arg2"
      name: "state_update_tool2"
```
and both of the tools will update he session state, respectively. then, only the last state update will be horned. 

**To Reproduce**
the following unit test will fail with the current implementation

```
async def test_parallel_function_calls_with_state_change():
  function_calls = [
      types.Part.from_function_call(
          name='update_session_state',
          args={'key': 'test_key1', 'value': 'test_value1'},
      ),
      types.Part.from_function_call(
          name='update_session_state',
          args={'key': 'test_key2', 'value': 'test_value2'},
      ),
      types.Part.from_function_call(
          name='transfer_to_agent', args={'agent_name': 'test_sub_agent'}
      ),
  ]
  function_responses = [
      types.Part.from_function_response(
          name='update_session_state', response={'result': None}
      ),
      types.Part.from_function_response(
          name='update_session_state', response={'result': None}
      ),
      types.Part.from_function_response(
          name='transfer_to_agent', response={'result': None}
      ),
  ]

  responses: list[types.Content] = [
      function_calls,
      'response1',
  ]
  function_called = 0
  mock_model = testing_utils.MockModel.create(responses=responses)

  async def update_session_state(
      key: str, value: str, tool_context: ToolContext
  ) -> None:
    nonlocal function_called
    function_called += 1
    tool_context.state.update({key: value})
    return

  async def transfer_to_agent(
      agent_name: str, tool_context: ToolContext
  ) -> None:
    nonlocal function_called
    function_called += 1
    tool_context.actions.transfer_to_agent = agent_name
    return

  test_sub_agent = Agent(
      name='test_sub_agent',
  )

  agent = Agent(
      name='root_agent',
      model=mock_model,
      tools=[update_session_state, transfer_to_agent],
      sub_agents=[test_sub_agent],
  )
  runner = testing_utils.TestInMemoryRunner(agent)
  events = await runner.run_async_with_new_session('test')

  # Notice that the following assertion only checks the "contents" part of the events.
  # The "actions" part will be checked later.
  assert testing_utils.simplify_events(events) == [
      ('root_agent', function_calls),
      ('root_agent', function_responses),
      ('test_sub_agent', 'response1'),
  ]

  # Asserts the function calls.
  assert function_called == 3

  # Asserts the actions in response event.
  response_event = events[1]

  assert response_event.actions == EventActions(
      state_delta={
          'test_key1': 'test_value1',
          'test_key2': 'test_value2',
      },
      transfer_to_agent='test_sub_agent',
  )

```


**Expected behavior**
EventAction from multiple function calls will be properly merged. 


**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Python version(python -V): 3.11.2
 - ADK version(pip show google-adk): 1.6.1

 **Additional Information:**
After carefully inspect the code, i found the root cause of the issue.  When there are multiple functions calls in the same event, ADK tries to merge the EventAction updates resulting from all the function calls (see: https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/src/google/adk/flows/llm_flows/functions.py#L537). However, the merging logic is wrong. it replaces the value instead of merging it when the type of the action field is `dict`. The handling of `requested_auth_configs` is correct though. 

Also, it seems that https://github.com/google/adk-python/issues/345 and https://github.com/google/adk-python/issues/1119 both related to this.

### I will create a PR that fix this properly that merging logic changes based on the data type. 
_For project owner: you can assign this issue to me._

linked_prs.body: This fixes https://github.com/google/adk-python/issues/1938

<div type='discussions-op-text'>

<sup>Originally posted by **chinarjoshi** April 11, 2023</sup>
Natural language to bash is a powerful tool that I believe deserves its own built in interface into the shell rather than a separate program. I propose an interface where users can toggle between natural language and English with a key binding to create a more user-friendly shell. Not to bash bash, but simple tasks should not take research on which program + flag combo will yield the right result with external programs like man and google. It is a more intuitive interface to toggle between a description and its command with a keybinding that invokes the sgpt program, rather than typing *sgpt -s "command"* every time. This is useful if you forget a flag midway through a command or want to figure out what a command does. Developers of any experience, especially people new to the terminal, frequently face this issue; thus, there must be an interface integrated directly with the shell to save both key presses and the cognitive load of another program.

### This interface behaves as such
Makes a key binding that transforms the content of the buffer based on what is currently in it, which has 4 cases:
1. Shell command -> natural language description
2. Natural language -> shell command
3. No text -> natural language description of previous command
4. If there is natural language in the buffer and the user presses enter, then the command is translated to shell before executing. If it is a non-destructive command, it is directly executed. Otherwise, the user is prompted before execution, just like the default behavior.

### This interface comprises of two changes
1. Shell script that is sourced by the users shell rc file that creates a keybinding that toggles the buffer using the sgpt program
2. New "--describe-shell" command that produces a single imperative sentence that describes a given shell command. This addresses  #118 .

Here is a demonstration of the described behavior. I will make a pull request containing these changes.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/68311366/232335365-0983ea04-4eb6-4c79-9eef-add798be93da.mp4

linked_prs.title: Shell integrations
linked_prs.body:
Implementation of #194 . The key-binding is Control+Space, which doesn't conflict on zsh nor bash.

I decided most commands *sgpt* spits out are good enough to execute directly without supervision. This makes the natural language interface really make it feel like an English shell. However, there are two hacks when executing a natural language command directly that should be discussed:
1. The way command_not_found_handler decides if its English is whether the first word is upper cased and there are at least 6 words in the sentence. I figured this because natural language is more verbose than bash, so an arbitrary length threshold is a good heuristic.
2. The way _sgpt_is_destructive_command checks if the command is destructive is manually check if its in the list (rm mv dd chmod sed git mkfs mkswap). There are of course many more destructive commands, and to be safe the script should be checking a wider range of them.

I also added a .gitignore file with GitHub's Python template because __pycache__ files kept being recognized by git.

If you agree with this interface, the next thing to do is update pyproject.toml to prompt the user to update their shell rc to source this shell script, and update documentation for the --describe-shell flag.

title: Model_adapter is case sensitive. This fails with downloaded models.
body:
Example: baichuan-inc/Baichuan-7B

It works when you use 
```python
model-path=baichuan-inc/Baichuan-7B
```
, but fails if you clone it and use like

```pyhton
model-path models/Baichuan-7B
```

Because all searches are case-sensitive, like for this one: 

https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat/blob/961b5de6f10b4c810062402995256f0ec704ff39/fastchat/model/model_adapter.py#L1068

As this fails, it will use a generic model adapter, which will fail, usually like this:

```
ValueError: Loading models/Baichuan-13B-Chat 
requires you to execute the tokenizer file in that repo on your local machine. 
Make sure you have read the code there to avoid malicious use, then set the 
option `trust_remote_code=True` to remove this error.
```

So, I would suggest two changes:

1) make the search case-insensitive
2) report which model template is being used when logging, for example:

This is today:
```python
2023-07-13 12:14:09 | INFO | model_worker | Loading the model ['Baichuan-13B-Chat'] on worker 2d7bb3f8 ...
```

I would use:

```python
2023-07-13 12:14:09 | INFO | model_worker | Loading the model ['Baichuan-13B-Chat'] using template GENERIC on worker 2d7bb3f8 ...
```

linked_prs.title: Fix model name selection when multiple servers use the same model
linked_prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #196 by improving the model name selection logic in `LLMProxy` to handle the case where multiple server configurations exist for the same model (e.g., for load balancing).

## Changes

- Modified `create_llm()` in `agentlightning/llm_proxy.py` to allow automatic model selection when all configured models have the same `model_name`, even if there are multiple server configurations
- Improved error messages to distinguish between "no models configured" and "multiple different models configured" cases
- Updated docstring to reflect the new behavior

## Problem

Previously, when multiple servers were configured to serve the same model (common in distributed setups like VERL), the code would fail with:
```
ValueError: Multiple or zero models found in model_list
```

This occurred even though all servers were serving the same logical model (e.g., `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`), just with different API endpoints for load balancing.

## Solution

The fix checks if all model configurations share the same `model_name`. If they do, that model name is automatically used, allowing the proxy to distribute requests across multiple servers serving the same model.

## Test plan

- Verify that single model configuration still works as before
- Verify that multiple servers with the same model name now work correctly
- Verify that multiple servers with different model names still require explicit model specification
- Verify that empty model_list produces a clear error message

title: Feature Request: add query and datetime filters to list_console_message tool
body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
The `list_console_messages` tool returns a number of unfiltered results (messages) back to the LLM.

This amounts to unnecessary build-up of irrelevant tokens for LLM context parsing / usage, thereby accumulating cost, not just in currency, but also in LLM processing speed inefficiencies, and potentially negatively impacting accuracy / relevance of LLM output results.

## Describe the solution you'd like
Add further filtering parameters, such as search query filtering on console messages by input -> `query`.

In addition, we could also filter on specific datetime ranges by allowing the LLM to provide ISO formatted input -> `from_datetime` and input -> `to_datetime` values.

This should extend the recent work applied in the following PRs:
- #183 

### Example 1 - Input -> `query`
- I add-in specifically formatted console messages (e.g. namespaced with "[some-file.ts]: ..."), and I ask then the LLM to search for and return all browser console messages which contains the above namespace. 
- The LLM makes the appropriate call to the console tool, and it will pass in the query filter input `query` 
- The MCP tool will return a specific subset of console messages only that were asked for by the me back to LLM for parsing without overloading / polluting the tool output response back to the LLM of all other irrelevant console message.

### Example 2 - Input -> `from_datetime` / input -> `to_datetime`
- The MCP controlled browser session has been running for like lets say 15 minutes already, and plenty of console.logs are general throughout that time as the browser goes through various interaction states. 
- I ask LLM to give me a summary of the logs that were generated over the last few minutes which is of my particular use-case / concern that I want to delve deeper into.
- The LLM will make the tool call and appropriately specify the above datetime inputs
- The MCP tool will respond with only the subset of console messages as per my request.

## Benefits
- Reduced LLM context token wastage, and by positive implication, cost ($)
- Reduced unnecessary parsing of additional irrelevant messages
- Reduction in unnecessary LLM noise / confusion, thus LLM analysis results / feedback
- May even improve speed of overall LLM output process, as there would be less messages to parse

title: Enhancement: Add updated_at tracking to hybrid backend sync
body:
## Problem

The hybrid backend's sync mechanism currently only detects **missing memories** (by `content_hash`) but does not sync **metadata updates** (tags, types, custom fields). This causes data drift when memories are updated on one backend but not synced to the other.

### Current Behavior

From `src/mcp_memory_service/storage/hybrid.py:711-716`:
```python
existing = await self.primary.get_by_hash(cf_memory.content_hash)
if not existing:
    # Memory doesn't exist locally, sync it
    success, message = await self.primary.store(cf_memory)
```

The sync checks if a memory exists by `content_hash` and **only syncs if missing**. It does NOT compare `updated_at` timestamps to detect metadata changes.

### Impact

- **Tag fixes** in Cloudflare don't propagate to local SQLite (discovered in tag repair issue)
- **Metadata updates** (`memory_type`, custom fields) can diverge between backends
- **Silent data loss** if update queue is full or service crashes
- No conflict detection when same memory updated on both backends

## Proposed Solution

Implement `updated_at` timestamp tracking in the hybrid sync:

### Changes Needed

1. **Track last sync timestamp** in hybrid backend state
2. **Modify `_perform_initial_sync()`** to detect drift:
   - After syncing missing memories, compare `updated_at` for existing memories
   - Re-sync memories where timestamps diverge
   - Use "newer timestamp wins" strategy
3. **Add new method `_detect_and_sync_drift()`**:
   - Query memories from both backends  
   - Compare `updated_at` for matching `content_hash`
   - Sync memories with divergent timestamps
4. **Enhance periodic sync** to check for updates since last sync:
   ```python
   updated_memories = await secondary.get_memories_updated_since(last_sync_time)
   for memory in updated_memories:
       if await primary.has_newer_version(memory):
           continue  # Local is newer, skip
       await primary.store(memory)  # Cloudflare is newer, update local
   ```

### Implementation Details

- Add `--dry-run` flag to preview changes
- Log all drift detections for audit trail
- Make opt-in with env var: `MCP_HYBRID_SYNC_UPDATES=true`
- Handle clock skew and timestamp conflicts

### Benefits

✅ Automatic metadata sync (tags, types, custom fields)  
✅ Bidirectional awareness (detects changes on either backend)  
✅ Conflict detection (knows when same memory updated on both sides)  
✅ Efficient (only syncs changed memories, not entire dataset)  
✅ Future-proof (handles all metadata update types)

## Research Context

The infrastructure already exists:
- Both backends store `updated_at` and `updated_at_iso` timestamps
- `SyncOperation` already supports `operation='update'`
- `update_memory_metadata()` queues updates to Cloudflare

The missing piece is using timestamps for sync decisions.

## Estimated Effort

**3-4 hours coding + 1 hour testing = Half day**

## Workaround (Immediate Fix)

Until implemented, users can run a full backup to sync current state:
```bash
uv run python scripts/sync/claude_sync_commands.py backup
```

---

**Related**: This enhancement prevents future occurrences of issues like the tag repair drift discovered today.

title: Support "@<agent name>" in addition to `/agent use`
body:
### Summary of the new feature / enhancement

In many other platforms including VSCode, and [clio](https://github.com/gptscript-ai/clio) the concept of scoping responses to specific agents or extensions is being done by prefixing responses with `@<scope>`, we should adopt a similar method where the user can run "@<agent> <optional query>" to switch between different agents and maintain that agent scope until user runs "@<different agent>". This helps reduce the number of commands users need to run to switch agents and get the right answer to their question, previously users would need to do `/agent use <x>` and then ask their question. 

### Proposed technical implementation details (optional)

Since there are landing page that agents provide, we need to surface these somehow to ensure users can understand the capabilities of the agent and see necessary links before beginning to use this agent. To get this behavior we need to show the landing page when the user only uses the `@agent` without a query and then only on first time use for `@agent <query>`. 

```powershell
<first time launch>
aish:1>@myAgent
This myAgents landing page...
myAgent:1>
<first time using myOtherAgent>
myAgent:2>@myOtherAgent "how are you today?"
This is myOtherAgents landing page

I am doing well, how are you?
myOtherAgent:1>
```

A complete user flow can be seen:
- User runs aish.exe 
- First time open up they select the agent like normal and current agent is used in the prompt
    - Continue to support configuration method to start aish with default agent
    - Landing page of that particular agent is visible and instructions to switch agents at the bottom with the instructions for /help 
- User can switch different agents using the "@" character
- Prompt and context are switched to that agent

```powershell
PS>aish.exe
AI Shell
0.1.0-alpha.12

Please select an agent to use:

> interpreter
  ollama
  openai-gpt

interpreter:1>
interpreter:2> @ollama how do I list files out?
 You can list files in a given directory using the  Get-ChildItem  cmdlet in PowerShell. Here's the command:

    Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\Your\Directory\Path"

  Replace  "C:\Your\Directory\Path"  with the path of the directory you want to list.

ollama:1>@openai-gpt
OpenAi-GPT Landing page
openai-gpt:1>

```
In the example above `ollama` agent has been used before and no longer needs to display the landing page.

title: Feature Request: Add Multi-Model Support to Claude Swarm
body:
## Overview

Enable Claude Swarm to orchestrate AI agents using any model/provider supported by the ruby_llm gem (OpenAI, Google Gemini, Cohere, etc.), extending beyond Claude-only swarms. This feature will allow teams to leverage the unique strengths of different AI models within a single collaborative swarm.

## Motivation

- **Model Diversity**: Different models excel at different tasks (e.g., GPT-4 for general reasoning, Gemini for multimodal tasks, specialized models for domain-specific work)
- **Cost Optimization**: Mix expensive high-capability models with cheaper alternatives based on task requirements
- **Vendor Independence**: Avoid lock-in to a single AI provider
- **Specialized Expertise**: Create swarms that combine Claude's coding abilities with other models' strengths

## Proposed Solution

### Architecture

Extend Claude Swarm to support non-Claude models by:
1. Running non-Claude instances as stdio-based MCP servers
2. Allowing Claude instances to connect to these servers via the existing MCP protocol
3. Providing a unified configuration interface that abstracts provider differences

### Configuration Schema

Extend the existing YAML configuration with optional provider-specific fields:

```yaml
version: 1
swarm:
  name: "Multi-Model Dev Team"
  main: lead
  instances:
    lead:
      description: "Claude Opus lead coordinating the team"
      directory: .
      model: opus
      connections: [gpt_analyst, gemini_designer]
      tools: [Read, Edit, Bash, mcp__gpt_analyst, mcp__gemini_designer]
      
    gpt_analyst:
      provider: openai           # New field (defaults to "claude")
      model: gpt-4-turbo
      api_key_env: OPENAI_API_KEY  # Optional: custom env var
      description: "GPT-4 for complex analysis and architecture"
      directory: ./src
      tools: [Read, Analyze]
      connections: [filesystem]
      
    gemini_designer:
      provider: google
      model: gemini-pro
      description: "Gemini for design and documentation"
      directory: ./docs
      tools: [Read, Edit, Write]
```

## Implementation Plan

### New Components

1. **`ClaudeSwarm::LlmMcpServer`** - MCP server implementation for LLM instances
2. **`ClaudeSwarm::LlmTaskTool`** - Primary tool for task execution
3. **`ClaudeSwarm::LlmExecutor`** - Abstraction over ruby_llm
4. **CLI command** - Add `llm-serve` alongside existing `mcp-serve`

### Modified Components

- **Configuration** - Add provider and api_key_env fields
- **Orchestrator** - Route non-Claude instances to LLM launcher
- **McpGenerator** - Generate correct MCP configs for LLM servers

## Technical Considerations

- API keys managed via environment variables
- Session management follows existing patterns
- Each LLM instance runs as separate process
- Tool compatibility varies by provider

## Example Use Cases

### Multi-Model Code Review
```yaml
instances:
  claude_dev:
    model: opus
    connections: [gpt_reviewer]
    
  gpt_reviewer:
    provider: openai
    model: gpt-4-turbo
    prompt: "You are a senior code reviewer"
```

### Cost-Optimized Development
```yaml
instances:
  main:
    model: sonnet  # Cheaper for coordination
    connections: [opus_expert, gpt_helper]
    
  gpt_helper:
    provider: openai
    model: gpt-3.5-turbo  # Cheap for simple tasks
```

## Backward Compatibility

- No breaking changes
- Provider defaults to "claude" when omitted
- Existing swarms work unchanged

## Dependencies

- ruby_llm gem for multi-provider support

## See Also

- Prototype implementations in comments below
- MCP Protocol: https://modelcontextprotocol.io

linked_prs.title: Add native streaming support for OpenAI clients
linked_prs.body:
## Description

This PR implements native streaming support for both OpenAI and Grok clients using the OpenAI SDK's streaming API. 

The implementation is based upon openai-go [examples](https://github.com/openai/openai-go/blob/main/examples/chat-completion-accumulating/main.go)

Previously, these clients were simulating streaming by making a single non-streaming call and returning an iterator that yielded just that response. 

https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubectl-ai/blob/69a1254cd2afd958e79e9900b797066e191ffd29/gollm/openai.go#L299-L341

This implementation replaces the simulation with true streaming that delivers tokens incrementally as they're generated by the API. 

## Changes Made

1. Updated the `SendStreaming` methods in both `openAIChatSession` and `grokChatSession` to use `NewStreaming` from the OpenAI Go SDK
2. Added proper accumulation of streaming chunks to build the complete message over time
3. Implemented handling for both text content and tool/function calls in streaming mode
4. Ensured conversation history is updated correctly after streaming completes
5. Added robust error handling for streaming responses
6. Implemented proper type handling for streaming-specific OpenAI types
7. Enhanced retry logic in `factory.go` for streaming connections

## Operation Modes

### Non-streaming Mode (existing behavior)

The `Send` method continues to work unchanged:
- Makes a single request to the LLM API using `Completions.New()`
- Waits for the entire response before returning
- Returns a single `ChatResponse` with complete text and/or function calls
- Updates the conversation history with the complete response

### Streaming Mode (new behavior)

The `SendStreaming` method now:
- Initializes a streaming connection with the LLM API using `Completions.NewStreaming()`
- Returns a `ChatResponseIterator` that yields chunks of the response as they arrive
- Uses the OpenAI SDK's `ChatCompletionAccumulator` to track the full response
- Processes both text and function call parts incrementally
- Updates the conversation history once streaming is complete

## Benefits

1. **Improved User Experience**: Responses appear progressively as they're generated
2. **Tool/Function Call Support**: Full compatibility with LLM tools/functions in streaming mode
3. **Resilience**: Better handling of long responses and potential connection issues
4. **API Efficiency**: Uses native streaming protocol
5. **Consistency**: Both OpenAI and Grok clients now use the same streaming implementation

## Testing

### qwen
I used #166 as reference and tested `qwen`, which now works!:

```

There is a bug with adk.models.lite_llm parsing the mimetype in a none compatible way. The current way works for openai provider which doesn't seem to use the mime type, but only look at the data. The issue occurs with gemini and anthropic (i haven't tested any other).

title: Issue: Inline data (base64) being stored in database and logged, causing performance and security issues.
body:
**Describe the bug**

Whenever files/attachments are added in the prompt and sent in the  LLM request. This is usually done in two ways, [inline_data / file_data](https://github.com/googleapis/python-genai/blob/main/google/genai/types.py#L972)  . In [google_llm.py](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/src/google/adk/models/google_llm.py#L47), inline_data is excluded from logging. 

But it is not excluded when using a database session service. Which leads to the following problems. 

1. Database Performance & Storage Issues

Database bloat: Base64 encoding increases file size by ~33%, causing unnecessary database growth
Query performance: Large blob data slows down database operations, queries, and backups
Memory consumption: Loading sessions with large inline_data consumes excessive memory
Storage costs: Database storage is significantly more expensive than object storage

2. Security & Privacy Concerns

Sensitive data exposure: File contents (PDFs, documents, images) are stored as plain text in database
Log pollution: The current logging logger.info[(In Database Session Service)](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/src/google/adk/sessions/database_session_service.py#L538C4-L538C66) dumps base64 data into logs.
Compliance risks: May violate data retention/privacy regulations (GDPR, HIPAA, etc.), as file storage has different rules compared to text logs. 
Log security: Logs are typically less secure than dedicated file storage systems

3. Operational Issues

Unreadable logs: Base64 data makes logs impossible to read and debug
Log storage costs: Logs become unnecessarily large
Backup complexity: Database backups become massive due to embedded files


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1.  Add a pdf/image through inline_data in the message parts.
2. Use a database_session_service (can start with a simple sqllite db) 
3. run it as a fast api server 
4. See the log pollution 

**Expected behavior**
There is support for [file_data in parts](https://github.com/googleapis/python-genai/blob/main/google/genai/types.py#L972) which we have to manage the files additionaly. 

 The inline_data should be excluded from logging anyway , similar to existing code in [google_llm.py](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/src/google/adk/models/google_llm.py#L47)


**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Python version(python -V): 3.13.2
 - ADK version(pip show google-adk):  1.7.0

 **Model Information:**
 Gemini 2.5 pro

**Additional context**

Followed the way how adk web supports the attachments, maybe it's fine for local development, but in production, usually to support this with a persistent db storage, inline_data should not be logged in the database, so supporting attachments through file_data seems the way to go forward. 

But it should also not pollute the logs.

linked_prs.body:
## Overview

Implements the **workflow_as_agent** reflection pattern - a complete Worker/Reviewer quality assurance system that iteratively improves agent responses through feedback loops.

**Closes #218** (workflow_as_agent pattern implementation)  
**Closes #219** (Add /v1/workflow/reflection API endpoint)

This PR consolidates all workflow_as_agent functionality including core pattern implementation, FastAPI backend, comprehensive documentation, and test coverage.

---

## What's New

### Core Workflow Pattern (`workflow_as_agent.py`)
- **WorkflowAgent** with Worker/Reviewer executors using Microsoft Agent Framework
- Worker generates responses, Reviewer evaluates against 4 quality criteria:
  - **Relevance**: Addresses the query
  - **Accuracy**: Factually correct
  - **Clarity**: Easy to understand
  - **Completeness**: Covers all aspects
- Iterative refinement loop until approval threshold met (avg score ≥ 4.0)
- Structured communication via `ReviewRequest`/`ReviewResponse` Pydantic models
- Full SSE streaming support via `run_stream()`

### FastAPI Backend (`haxui/api.py` & `haxui/runtime.py`)
- **POST /v1/workflow/reflection** - Dedicated endpoint for reflection workflow
- Real-time SSE streaming of Worker responses, Reviewer feedback, iterations
- Full conversation management API (create, list, get, delete)
- Entity discovery endpoint for frontend agent/workflow catalog
- Modern FastAPI lifespan pattern for clean async initialization
- Comprehensive error handling (400, 404, 500 status codes)
- `FleetRuntime` with lazy initialization and entity catalog
- Custom model selection (worker_model, reviewer_model parameters)

### HaxUI Foundation
- **Conversation management** (`conversations.py`) - In-memory store with OpenAI-compatible API
- **Pydantic models** (`models.py`) - EntityInfo, ConversationSummary, HealthResponse
- **Web approval handler** (`web_approval.py`) - SSE-compatible HITL integration
- **UI assets** - Frontend entry point (`index.html`) and icons

### Type Safety Fixes
- **`mem0_provider.py`**: Fixed Path vs str handling with proper type annotations
  - Moved imports to top of file (resolved E402 errors)
  - Proper `Path.expanduser().resolve()` usage

---

## API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `/v1/workflow/reflection` | POST | Execute reflection workflow with SSE streaming |
| `/health` | GET | Health check |
| `/v1/entities` | GET | Discover available agents and workflows |
| `/v1/conversations` | POST/GET | Create and list conversations |
| `/v1/conversations/{id}` | GET/DELETE | Get or delete specific conversation |
| `/v1/conversations/{id}/items` | GET | Retrieve conversation message history |

---

## Request/Response Format

**Request:**
```json
{
  "query": "Your question here",
  "worker_model": "gpt-4.1-nano",      // optional
  "reviewer_model": "gpt-4.1",         // optional
  "conversation_id": "conv_abc123"     // optional
}
```

**SSE Response Stream:**
```json
{"type": "response.output_text.delta", "delta": "text chunk", ...}
{"type": "response.done", "conversation_id": "conv_123", "usage": {...}}
```

---

title: Bug on 2 conversation templates
body:
Hello, after some research I noticed that 2 (Starchat and Llama2) of your prompt templates are slightly wrong:

For starchat, in fastchat/conversations.py line 820:
```python
# StarChat template
register_conv_template(
    Conversation(
        name="starchat",
        system_template="<system>{system_message}\n",  # WRONG HERE
        roles=("<|user|>", "<|assistant|>"),
        messages=(),
        offset=0,
        sep_style=SeparatorStyle.CHATML,
        sep="<|end|>",
        stop_token_ids=[0, 49155],
        stop_str="<|end|>",
    )
)
```

should be (see also https://huggingface.co/spaces/HuggingFaceH4/starchat-playground/blob/main/dialogues.py)

```python
# StarChat template
register_conv_template(
    Conversation(
        name="starchat",
        system_template="<system>\n{system_message}",  # CORRECT HERE
        roles=("<|user|>", "<|assistant|>"),
        messages=(),
        offset=0,
        sep_style=SeparatorStyle.CHATML,
        sep="<|end|>",
        stop_token_ids=[0, 49155],
        stop_str="<|end|>",
    )
)
```


and for llama2, in fastchat/conversations.py line 123:

```python
elif self.sep_style == SeparatorStyle.LLAMA2:
    seps = [self.sep, self.sep2]
    ret = ""
    for i, (role, message) in enumerate(self.messages):
        if message:
            if i == 0:
                ret += system_prompt + message # WRONG HERE
            else:
                ret += role + " " + message + seps[i % 2]
        else:
            ret += role
    return ret
````

should be (see also https://github.com/facebookresearch/llama/blob/main/llama/generation.py#L212)

```python
elif self.sep_style == SeparatorStyle.LLAMA2:
    seps = [self.sep, self.sep2]
    ret = ""
    for i, (role, message) in enumerate(self.messages):
        if message:
            if i == 0:
                ret += system_prompt + message + ' ' # CORRECT HERE
            else:
                ret += role + " " + message + seps[i % 2]
        else:
            ret += role
    return ret
```

If you agree that both are mistakes, I can quickly correct the code and create a PR if you want.

title: Function calling issue with gpt-oss
body:
While `[gpt-oss:20b](https://ollama.com/blog/gpt-oss)` generally works, e.g. for task summaries, it only partially works for creating checklist items, only one item is created at the time. 

# GPT-OSS Models Only Process Single Function Calls Instead of Batches in Ollama

## Issue Summary
When using GPT-OSS models (gpt-oss-120b / gpt-oss-20b) with Ollama for function calling, the models consistently process only one item at a time, even when explicitly instructed to handle multiple items. This forces users to manually re-prompt for each additional item in what should be a single batch operation.

## Environment
- **Models**: gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b (OpenAI open-weight models, August 2025 release)
- **Runtime**: Ollama v0.7+ with OpenAI compatibility mode
- **Format**: GGUF quantized versions (Q2-Q8)
- **API**: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with tools parameter

## Root Cause: Response Format Incompatibility

### 1. Harmony Format vs OpenAI Format
GPT-OSS models use OpenAI's "harmony response format" which includes multiple channels:
```
<|channel|>analysis
[reasoning trace and CoT]
<|channel|>final
[actual response with function calls]
```

Ollama's OpenAI compatibility layer expects standard format:
```json
{
  "tool_calls": [
    {
      "id": "call_xyz",
      "type": "function",
      "function": {"name": "...", "arguments": "..."}
    }
  ]
}
```

### 2. Parser Failures
The models often output function calls as plain text within message content:
```
{"name": "create_task", "parameters": {"title": "Buy milk"}}
{"name": "create_task", "parameters": {"title": "Call dentist"}}
```

But Ollama's parser expects properly structured `tool_calls` arrays, resulting in:
- Empty `tool_calls=[]` responses
- Function calls treated as regular text
- Only first function call being recognized (if any)

### 3. Known Ollama Limitations
- **Experimental OpenAI compatibility**: Marked as "subject to major adjustments including breaking changes"
- **Limited JSON Schema support**: Only subset of JSON Schema features supported
- **No true batch processing**: Ollama processes requests sequentially even with `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL`
- **GGUF quantization effects**: Lower quantization levels (Q2-Q4) significantly degrade structured output generation

## Symptoms
1. **Malformed tool calls** (Issue #11704): Function names contain template artifacts like `assistant<|channel|>analysis`
2. **Format degradation**: JSON structure breaks when attempting multiple function calls
3. **Silent failures**: Model acknowledges multiple items in reasoning but only processes one
4. **Inconsistent behavior**: Same prompt produces different results across runs

## Reproduction Steps
1. Load GPT-OSS model in Ollama: `ollama pull gpt-oss:120b`
2. Send request with multiple function calls:
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-oss:120b",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Create tasks for: buy milk, call dentist, review code"}],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {...}}]
}
```
3. Observe: Only first task gets created, requiring manual re-prompting for others

## Related Issues
- ollama/ollama#11704 - Malformed tool calls with GPT-OSS
- ollama/ollama#7572 - OpenAI API tool calling doesn't work
- ollama/ollama#6377 - Limited JSON Schema support
- vllm-project/vllm#22337 - GPT-OSS tool call compatibility

## Current Workarounds
1. Process items sequentially with explicit single-item prompts
2. Use higher quantization models (Q6-Q8) for better structured output
3. Implement retry logic with format validation
4. Consider alternative models optimized for Ollama (e.g., llama3-groq-tool-use)

## Expected Behavior
Model should process all requested items in a single response, returning multiple function calls in the `tool_calls` array.

## Actual Behavior
Model processes only one item per request, requiring N separate API calls for N items, significantly impacting performance and user experience.

## Impact
This limitation makes GPT-OSS models impractical for production use cases requiring batch operations, such as task management, bulk data processing, or any workflow involving multiple function calls.

> Hello, I am the user that reported [#165](https://github.com/google-a2a/a2a-python/issues/165). I am still facing the problem as they answered me and closed the issue but it's not working with the suggested solution. Hope we have it solved soon🤞 

 _Originally posted by @alberto-atk in [#220](https://github.com/google-a2a/a2a-python/issues/220#issuecomment-2990192346)_


Currently, the only solution is to modify the SDK code directly, specifically in `jsonrpc_app.py`, to use `by_alias=True` as shown below:

```python
async def _handle_get_agent_card(self, request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    """
    Handles GET requests for the agent card endpoint.

    Args:
        request: The incoming Starlette Request object.

    Returns:
        A JSONResponse containing the agent card data.
    """
    # The public agent card is directly serialized from the agent_card provided at initialization.
    return JSONResponse(
        self.agent_card.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
```

It would be great if they could update the SDK to implement this fix, so we don't have to manually alter the code in the release environment.

Users were encountering cryptic HTTP 400 errors when manually setting `deploymentId` in `start()` options, a parameter that should be auto-inferred from environment variables in production.

## Changes

- Marked `StartOptions.deploymentId` as `@deprecated` with TSDoc
- Added inline documentation clarifying:
  - Property is auto-inferred from `VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_ID` 
  - Should not be set in user code
  - Only override for advanced use cases

## Example

IDEs will now show deprecation warnings when users attempt to use this parameter:

```typescript
import { start } from 'workflow';
import * as myWorkflow from './workflows/my-workflow';

// ❌ IDE shows deprecation warning
await start(myWorkflow, [], { deploymentId: 'some-id' });

// ✅ Correct usage - deploymentId auto-inferred
await start(myWorkflow, []);
```

title: Bug: WebSocket-native MCP tools return no output (silent failure)
body:
## Summary

WebSocket-native Genie MCP tools return no output when called, making it impossible to verify if they succeeded or failed. This violates the principle that tools should provide feedback about their results.

## Affected Tools

Based on MCP server documentation, these tools use WebSocket transport:
- `mcp__genie__create_wish(feature, github_issue)`
- `mcp__genie__run_forge(prompt, agent)`
- `mcp__genie__run_review(wish_name, agent)`
- `mcp__genie__transform_prompt(prompt, agent)`

## Observed Behavior

**When called:**
```
mcp__genie__create_wish(
  feature="Fix infinite update loop...",
  github_issue=237
)
```

**Result:**
```
<system>Tool ran without output or errors</system>
```

**Questions:**
1. Did the wish get created? Unknown.
2. What's the wish slug? Unknown.
3. What's the Forge task ID? Unknown.
4. How do I verify it worked? Unknown.

## Expected Behavior

Tools should return:
1. **Success confirmation:** "Wish created: wish-237-fix-infinite-update-loop"
2. **Task/session ID:** For tracking and verification
3. **URL to view:** Forge UI link or session info
4. **OR explicit error:** If operation failed

## Impact

**User Impact:**
- Cannot verify if operations succeeded
- No way to track created tasks/wishes
- Forces manual verification (Forge UI, list_sessions)
- Breaks automation workflows

**Agent Impact:**
- Cannot mark tasks "completed" with evidence (Learning #13)
- Must assume success/failure blindly
- Cannot implement proper error handling
- Violates "evidence-based completion" protocol

## Reproduction

1. Start Genie MCP server
2. Call any WebSocket-native tool
3. Observe: No output returned
4. Check Forge UI manually to see if operation succeeded

## Possible Root Causes

1. **WebSocket streaming not visible in Claude Code:**
   - Output streams via WebSocket
   - Claude Code only shows final result
   - No final result message sent

2. **Tools designed for UI, not API:**
   - Meant to be viewed in Forge dashboard
   - Not designed for programmatic use
   - Missing return values

3. **Incomplete MCP implementation:**
   - Tools missing result serialization
   - Forgot to send response message
   - Bug in WebSocket handler

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Return Session/Task ID
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "task_id": "abc123",
  "session_id": "wish-237-genie-20251023",
  "forge_url": "http://localhost:8887/tasks/abc123"
}
```

### Option 2: Return Status Message
```
✅ Wish created: wish-237-fix-infinite-update-loop
📋 Forge task: http://localhost:8887/tasks/abc123
🔍 Track progress: mcp__genie__view("wish-237-genie-20251023")
```

### Option 3: Make Tools Synchronous
- Wait for operation to complete
- Return final result
- Trade: slower but verifiable

## Workarounds

**Current workarounds:**
1. Use `mcp__genie__list_sessions` after calling tool
2. Check Forge UI manually
3. Use non-WebSocket alternatives where available
4. Grep filesystem for new wish directories

**These workarounds are inadequate:**
- Extra API calls for every operation
- No guarantee operation completed
- Breaks automation workflows
- Violates evidence-based protocols

## Related

- Learning #11: WebSocket Tool Silent Failures Protocol
- Learning #13: Evidence-Based Todo Completion
- Issue #237: Update loop investigation (where this bug was discovered)

## Discovery Context

Discovered while trying to create debug wish for issue #237. Tool returned no output, marked task "completed" anyway (protocol violation). User noticed: "i saw not everything worked as expected".

This bug prevents proper evidence-based completion protocols from working.

title: User-defined tool descriptions
body: Users should be able to customize individual (or all) tool descriptions at server startup.

linked_prs.title: feat: add a framework for translations
linked_prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/issues/24

## i18n / Overriding descriptions
The descriptions of the tools can be overridden by creating a github-mcp-server.json file in the same directory as the binary.
The file should contain a JSON object with the tool names as keys and the new descriptions as values.
For example:
```json
{
  "TOOL_ADD_ISSUE_COMMENT_DESCRIPTION": "an alternative description",
  "TOOL_CREATE_BRANCH_DESCRIPTION": "Create a new branch in a GitHub repository"
}
```
You can create an export of the current translations by running the binary with the `--export-translations` flag.
This flag will preserve any translations/overrides you have made, while adding any new translations that have been added to the binary since the last time you exported.
```sh
./github-mcp-server --export-translations
cat github-mcp-server.json
```
You can also use ENV vars to override the descriptions. The environment variable names are the same as the keys in the JSON file,
prefixed with `GITHUB_MCP_` and all uppercase.
For example, to override the `TOOL_ADD_ISSUE_COMMENT_DESCRIPTION` tool, you can set the following environment variable:
```sh
export GITHUB_MCP_TOOL_ADD_ISSUE_COMMENT_DESCRIPTION="an alternative description"
```

### The JSON Dump

So far, I have drawn the line at descriptions, but parameters can easily be added, I just didn't want this PR to touch any more parts. This is the whole shebang:

```json
{
  "RESOURCE_REPOSITORY_CONTENT_BRANCH_DESCRIPTION": "Repository Content for specific branch",
  "RESOURCE_REPOSITORY_CONTENT_COMMIT_DESCRIPTION": "Repository Content for specific commit",
  "RESOURCE_REPOSITORY_CONTENT_DESCRIPTION": "Repository Content",
  "RESOURCE_REPOSITORY_CONTENT_PR_DESCRIPTION": "Repository Content for specific pull request",
  "RESOURCE_REPOSITORY_CONTENT_TAG_DESCRIPTION": "Repository Content for specific tag",
  "TOOL_ADD_ISSUE_COMMENT_DESCRIPTION": "Add a comment to an existing issue",
  "TOOL_CREATE_BRANCH_DESCRIPTION": "Create a new branch in a GitHub repository",
  "TOOL_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FILE_DESCRIPTION": "Create or update a single file in a GitHub repository",
  "TOOL_CREATE_REPOSITORY_DESCRIPTION": "Create a new GitHub repository in your account",
  "TOOL_FORK_REPOSITORY_DESCRIPTION": "Fork a GitHub repository to your account or specified organization",
  "TOOL_GET_CODE_SCANNING_ALERT_DESCRIPTION": "Get details of a specific code scanning alert in a GitHub repository.",
  "TOOL_GET_FILE_CONTENTS_DESCRIPTION": "Get the contents of a file or directory from a GitHub repository",
  "TOOL_GET_ISSUE_DESCRIPTION": "Get details of a specific issue in a GitHub repository.",
  "TOOL_GET_ME_DESCRIPTION": "Get details of the authenticated GitHub user",
  "TOOL_GET_PULL_REQUEST_COMMENTS_DESCRIPTION": "Get the review comments on a pull request",
  "TOOL_GET_PULL_REQUEST_DESCRIPTION": "Get details of a specific pull request",
  "TOOL_GET_PULL_REQUEST_FILES_DESCRIPTION": "Get the list of files changed in a pull request",
  "TOOL_GET_PULL_REQUEST_REVIEWS_DESCRIPTION": "Get the reviews on a pull request",
  "TOOL_GET_PULL_REQUEST_STATUS_DESCRIPTION": "Get the combined status of all status checks for a pull request",
  "TOOL_LIST_CODE_SCANNING_ALERTS_DESCRIPTION": "List code scanning alerts in a GitHub repository.",
  "TOOL_LIST_COMMITS_DESCRIPTION": "Get list of commits of a branch in a GitHub repository",
  "TOOL_LIST_PULL_REQUESTS_DESCRIPTION": "List and filter repository pull requests",
  "TOOL_MERGE_PULL_REQUEST_DESCRIPTION": "Merge a pull request",
  "TOOL_SEARCH_CODE_DESCRIPTION": "Search for code across GitHub repositories",
  "TOOL_SEARCH_ISSUES_DESCRIPTION": "Search for issues and pull requests across GitHub repositories",
  "TOOL_SEARCH_REPOSITORIES_DESCRIPTION": "Search for GitHub repositories",
  "TOOL_SEARCH_USERS_DESCRIPTION": "Search for GitHub users",
  "TOOL_UPDATE_PULL_REQUEST_BRANCH_DESCRIPTION": "Update a pull request branch with the latest changes from the base branch"
}
```

### Live example `tools/list`

An example running with a file, and an env var:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "result": {
    "tools": [
      {
        "description": "an alternative description",
        "inputSchema": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "body": {
              "description": "Comment text",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "issue_number": {
              "description": "Issue number to comment on",
              "type": "number"
            },
            "owner": {
              "description": "Repository owner",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "repo": {
              "description": "Repository name",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "owner",
            "repo",
            "issue_number",
            "body"
          ]
        },
        "name": "add_issue_comment"
      },
      {
        "description": "OVERRIDE DESCRIPTION",
        "inputSchema": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "branch": {
              "description": "Name for new branch",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "from_branch": {
              "description": "Source branch (defaults to repo default)",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "owner": {
              "description": "Repository owner",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "repo": {
              "description": "Repository name",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "owner",
            "repo",
            "branch"
          ]
        },
        "name": "create_branch"
      },
      ...
    ]
  }
}

```

ai_judgment.response:
Yes.  
This is an agent issue because it concerns tool configuration—specifically, the ability to customize tool descriptions at startup, which directly affects how tools are defined and presented within the agent system. This aligns with the "Tool configuration issues" sub-category.

linked_prs.body:
fixes: #250

- What was wrong:
- Chat kept thinking legitimate responses were just "echoing" user input
- Generic "sorry I can't help" messages instead of useful guidance  
- Conversation history getting wiped out too aggressively

- What I improved:
- **Smarter echo detection** - Now correctly identifies when AI is actually just repeating vs providing real responses
- **Better fallback messages** - Users now get actionable suggestions like "provide more specific details" instead of generic apologies
- **Preserved conversation context** - Only removes problematic responses, keeps useful history intact
- **Cleaner code** - Removed unnecessary comments while keeping clarity

## Summary by Sourcery

Refine chat service to avoid false echo detections, provide more helpful fallback messages, and preserve conversation context while improving logging and code clarity

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent valid AI responses from being misidentified as echoes
