<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

### PR Summary

Fix #360

Update model information to support the new OpenAI models.

- The OpenAI reasoning models do not support the `temperature` setting -- they error out if you set the value. But the `DeepSeek R1` OpenAI compatible API still allows passing the `temperature` setting even though it has not effect.

- I don't have access to the `o3` model (requires verifying organization), but I've verified the changes with `o1`, `o3-mini`, `o4-mini`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4.1-mini`, and `gpt-4.1-nano` modules and it works fine.

- The `o1-mini` model doesn't work because it doesn't support the system prompt (very weird). Given that the `o3-mini` is out and recommended, I think it's fine to not work with `o1-mini`.

Regarding the reasoning/thinking tokens:

- The OpenAI reasoning models do not expose the Chain of Thoughts (CoT) tokens. They may provide a summary but that is not available with the `Chat Completion APIs` ([see details here](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/reasoning?api-mode=chat#reasoning-summaries)).

- The `DeepSeek R1` exposes the CoT tokens and has a really nice way of dealing with it in their version of OpenAI compatible `Chat Completion APIs` (see its [reasoning model doc](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/reasoning_model) for details). However, the .NET OpenAI SDK doesn't expose `reasoning_content` today. The tracking issue is https://github.com/openai/openai-dotnet/issues/259#issuecomment-2614483337
   > reasoning_content：The content of the CoT, which is at the same level as content in the output structure.

- The `Gemini` thinking models also exposes the CoT tokens but is limited with the OpenAI compatible APIs today. See https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/reasoning-tokens-combined-with-completion-tokens-in-openai-compatibility-mode/58354/7?utm_source=chatgpt.com for details. It may support exposing CoT tokens with the same way as `DeepSeek R1` in future.

We will work on supporting the CoT tokens once .NET OpenAI SDK is fixed to expose the `reasoning_content` field.

title: Native tool read_file_multi: pattern in JSON Schema is not standard-compliant
body:
### Plugin Type

VSCode Extension

### App Version

v4.117.0

### Description

#### **Summary**

In the native tool definition for `read_file_multi`, the `line_ranges` property uses a `pattern` with the regular expression `^\\d+-\\d+$`.

The `\d` shorthand is not part of the standard regular expression dialect supported by [JSON Schema (ECMA 262)](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/regular_expressions). This causes validation to fail in parsers that strictly follow the specification.

#### **Affected Code**

The issue is located in this line:
https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/blob/b9bcc48f846a82e28f0415bf1d436a4091e2f968/src/core/prompts/tools/native-tools/read_file.ts#L29

#### **Why it's a problem**

1.  **Non-standard compliance:** JSON Schema specifies that regular expressions must conform to the ECMA 262 dialect, which does not include the `\d` shorthand for digits.
2.  **Breaks Tool Usage:** This non-compliance is not theoretical. It prevents the tool from being used with backends that rely on strict schema validation. For instance, an API call with this tool will fail when using `llama.cpp`, as its GBNF grammar parser cannot handle the non-standard `\d` token. This blocking issue is demonstrated in [ggml-org/llama.cpp#16714](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/16714).

#### **Suggested Solution**

Replace `\\d` with the equivalent and standard-compliant character class `[0-9]`.

**Example fix:**

```diff
- pattern: "^\\d+-\\d+$",
+ pattern: "^[0-9]+-[0-9]+$",
```

#### **Expected Outcome**

After this change, the schema will be fully compliant with the JSON Schema standard. This will fix the integration with strict parsers like `llama.cpp`'s and improve the overall reliability of the tool.

### Reproduction steps

1.  Set up a `llama.cpp` server, version `b6970`.
2.  Load the `unsloth/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf`.
3.  Start the server.
4.  Configure `kilocode` to use this local server endpoint.
5.  Start `kilocode` in `code` mode and open a project with at least two files.
6.  Ask the model to read parts of multiple files, for example: *"Read lines 1-5 of `file1.ts` and lines 10-15 of `file2.ts`."*

### Provider

OpenAI Compatible via llama-server

### Model

unsloth/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf

### System Information

OS: Windows 11
CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 7700
GPU: x2 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti
RAM: 128GB DDR5

title: Introducing Looping Heuristics / Detection
body:
### Duplicates

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Summary 💡

This is a "meta" issue to keep track of issues relating to redundant/unnecessary (infinite/endless) looping and the idea to keep track of previous arguments to detect such situations, as per: https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT/issues/3444#issuecomment-1529005391


- https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT/issues/1994
- https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT/issues/3444
- https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT/issues/3644


Idea: maintain a "call stack" that contains hashed values of each query/prompt - whenever this is used, increment a counter to detect if we're inside a loop without making much progress (the arguments will remain the same, and so will the hash) - if we are not making any progress at all, the response will also be the same (hash that too).

This should also help the agent determine if it's trying to re-solve a task that was previously tackled.

Solution: For a sub-agent, it should notify its parent agent using either the messaging API or by throwing the equivalent of an exception, so that it can be terminated/restarted: https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT/issues/1548#issuecomment-1529009589

For top-level agents, it's probably best to interrupt the loop and pursue an alternate option - which may involve human feedback: https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT/issues/3396
The cleanest method might be offering a list of options to the user (inspired by the current state of things, as per #1548), including an option for open ended feedback.

This feedback should be serialized in some form, so that the agent can easily refer back to it as per: https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT/issues/1377
The goal being to provide a means to do some form of self-assessment, as per: #305 
This may involve telling the agent to log its progress to a task specific log file so that a parent agent can evaluate the log file, comparing it to the stated long-term goal.


### Examples 🌈

This is just based on hashing full thoughts + new decision (command + args) and incrementing a counter every time we get to see the same "situation":
![bailout](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT/assets/119627414/80fb2d00-37ea-4c59-9f73-0b6f58486142)

### Motivation 🔦

- detect whether an agent is trying to tackle a task that it tackled previously
- detect whether it's using the same arguments and seeing the same response (=being stuck)
- get rid of unnecessary looping
- allow an agent to detect whether its work is in line with the stated goal or not
- provide a means to bail out if necessary, either informing the parent agent and/or asking for human feedback
- at the very least, use this as a means to change the problem solving strategy

## Summary
This PR adds support for the OpenCUA models from xlangai along with InternVL 3.5 and Holo 1.5 grounding. It also updates the docs to reflect the full Model Zoo with consistent listings and cross-links.

## Models
- **Holo 1.5 (Grounding)**
  - `huggingface-local/Hcompany/Holo1.5-{3B,7B,72B}`
- **OpenCUA (Grounding + End-to-end)**
  - `huggingface-local/xlangai/OpenCUA-7B`
  - `huggingface-local/xlangai/OpenCUA-32B`
- **InternVL 3.5 (Grounding + End-to-end)**
  - `huggingface-local/OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-{1B,2B,4B,8B,...}`

## Usage

### via CLI
```bash
# OpenCUA — End-to-end Agent
python -m agent.cli huggingface-local/xlangai/OpenCUA-7B
python -m agent.cli huggingface-local/xlangai/OpenCUA-32B

# OpenCUA — Composed Agent using OpenCUA's GUI Grounding + a planner
python -m agent.cli huggingface-local/xlangai/OpenCUA-7B+openai/gpt-5

# InternVL 3.5 — End-to-end Agent
python -m agent.cli huggingface-local/OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-1B

# InternVL 3.5 — Composed Agent (use InternVL for grounding)
python -m agent.cli huggingface-local/OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-1B+anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022

# Holo 1.5 — Click prediction (grounding only)
python -m agent.cli huggingface-local/Hcompany/Holo1.5-7B --predict-click "start button"
```

### via SDK
```python
from agent import ComputerAgent

# OpenCUA — GUI Grounding
agent = ComputerAgent(model="huggingface-local/xlangai/OpenCUA-7B", tools=[computer])
coords = await agent.predict_click("start button")

# OpenCUA — End-to-end Agent (Composed)
agent = ComputerAgent(model="huggingface-local/xlangai/OpenCUA-7B+openai/gpt-5", tools=[computer])
async for _ in agent.run("create a spreadsheet with mock sales data using LibreOffice"):
    pass

# InternVL 3.5 — End-to-end Agent
agent = ComputerAgent(model="huggingface-local/OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-1B", tools=[computer])
async for _ in agent.run("Open Firefox and navigate to github.com"):
    pass

async for _ in agent.run("Open Firefox and navigate to github.com"):
    pass

# Holo 1.5 — GUI Grounding
agent = ComputerAgent(model="huggingface-local/Hcompany/Holo1.5-7B", tools=[computer])
coords = await agent.predict_click("start button")

async for _ in agent.run("Open Firefox and navigate to github.com"):
```

title: fix: prompt tagged template literal does not resolve non-ui template expressions
body:
## Problem Description

The `prompt` tagged template literal currently does not resolve template expressions that are outside of `<ui>` blocks. When using the `prompt` function with interpolated values outside of UI blocks, the placeholders remain as `__HBX_*__` tokens in the final compiled output instead of being replaced with their actual values.

## Current Behavior

When using template expressions outside of `<ui>` blocks:

```typescript
const docs = [
  { url: '/docs/intro', title: 'Introduction' },
  { url: '/docs/api', title: 'API Reference' }
];

const sys = prompt`
  ## Available Documentation
  
  \`\`\`json
  ${JSON.stringify(docs, null, 2)}
  \`\`\`
  
  <ui><SearchResult url="/docs/intro" title="Introduction" /></ui>
`;

const compiled = sys.compile(components, schema);

```

**Result:** The compiled string contains `__HBX_0__` instead of the JSON data:

```

## Available Documentation

\`\`\`json
__HBX_0__
\`\`\`
```

## Expected Behavior

Template expressions outside of `<ui>` blocks should be resolved to their actual values:

```
## Available Documentation

\`\`\`json
[
  {
    "url": "/docs/intro",
    "title": "Introduction"
  },
  {
    "url": "/docs/api",
    "title": "API Reference"
  }
]
\`\`\`
```

While preserving the existing behavior for template expressions **inside** `<ui>` blocks, which need to remain as placeholder tokens for proper component validation and type checking.

## Root Cause

The `prompt` function uses `weavePlaceholders()` to replace template expressions with stable placeholder tokens (`__HBX_0__`, `__HBX_1__`, etc.) during parsing. These placeholders are only resolved within `<ui>` blocks by the component lowering system (`lowerToHB()` and `lowerWithPolicy()`).

Placeholders outside of `<ui>` blocks are never replaced, remaining as literal `__HBX_*__` tokens in the final output.

## Example Use Cases

### 1. Documentation Search System
```typescript
const docs = await loadDocs();

const system = prompt`
  You are a search assistant.
  
  ## Documentation Source
  ${docs}
  
  <ui><SearchResult url="/docs" title="Title" /></ui>
`;
```

### 2. Dynamic Configuration
```typescript
const config = { apiUrl: 'https://api.example.com', timeout: 5000 };

const system = prompt`
  Configuration: ${config}
  
  <ui><StatusMessage type="info" /></ui>
`;
```

### 3. Contextual Data Injection
```typescript
const metadata = { user: 'Alice', role: 'admin' };

const system = prompt`
  User: ${metadata.user}
  Role: ${metadata.role}
  
  <ui><UserCard name="${metadata.user}" /></ui>
`;
```

linked_prs.body:
*Closes https://github.com/IQAIcom/adk-ts/issues/373 when this PR merged*


Fix state variable injection in instructions to properly handle objects and nested properties

## Summary

Fixed two critical issues in the state variable injection system:
1. **Object serialization**: Objects were being converted to `"[object Object]"` instead of proper JSON
2. **Nested property access**: Syntax like `{basket.fruits[0].name}` was not being parsed

## Changes Made

### Core Implementation
**File: `packages/adk/src/utils/instructions-utils.ts`**

Added helper functions:
1. **`getNestedValue(obj, path)`** - Parses and accesses nested properties
   - Supports dot notation: `user.profile.firstName`
   - Supports bracket notation: `basket.fruits[0].name`
   - Handles quoted property names: `obj['key-name']` or `obj["another.key"]`
   - Properly handles keys containing dots or special characters
   - Uses character-by-character parsing to handle complex cases

2. **`formatValue(value)`** - Properly formats values for injection
   - Primitives (string, number, boolean) → String conversion
   - Objects and Arrays → `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)`
   - Handles null and undefined correctly

3. **Updated `replaceMatch()`** - Enhanced logic with security improvements:
   - Validates root property name even for nested paths (security fix)
   - Detects nested property access (contains `.` or `[`)
   - Uses `getNestedValue()` for nested paths
   - Uses `formatValue()` instead of `String()` for all values
   - **CRITICAL FIX**: Corrected regex from `/[.[]/` to `/[.\[]/` to properly escape the opening bracket (security vulnerability)

### Test Coverage
**File: `packages/adk/src/tests/utils/instructions-utils.test.ts`** (new)

Comprehensive test suite with 19 test cases:
- ✅ Primitive value injection (strings, numbers, booleans)
- ✅ Object JSON serialization
- ✅ Array JSON serialization  
- ✅ Nested object properties (`user.profile.firstName`)
- ✅ Array element access (`basket.fruits[0].name`)
- ✅ Deep nested access (`basket.fruits[1].color`)
- ✅ Multiple nested properties in one template
- ✅ Optional variables with `?` suffix
- ✅ Edge cases:
  - Null and undefined values
  - Invalid variable names
  - Root property validation for nested paths
  - Quoted property names in bracket notation

## Critical Security Fix (Latest Commit)

**Issue Identified by Claude Code Review**: 
- **Line 107**: Regex `/[.[]/` had an invalid character class
- **Problem**: The dot was not escaped, causing potential incorrect root property extraction
- **Impact**: Could bypass validation checks for malicious property paths
- **Fix**: Changed to `/[.\[]/` to properly escape the opening bracket

This ensures root property names are correctly extracted and validated, preventing security bypasses.

## Verification Results

✅ **All 283 tests passing** 
✅ **Code formatted** with Biome
✅ **Build successful** 
✅ **No breaking changes** to existing functionality
✅ **Security vulnerability addressed**

## Examples

### Before Fix
```typescript
state = { user: { name: "Alice", age: 30 } }
template = "User: {user}"
result = "User: [object Object]"  ❌

state = { basket: { fruits: [{ name: "apple" }] } }
template = "First fruit: {basket.fruits[0].name}"
result = "First fruit: {basket.fruits[0].name}"  ❌
```

```typescript
state = { user: { name: "Alice", age: 30 } }

}`  ✅

state = { basket: { fruits: [{ name: "apple" }] } }

```

title: [Bug]: Serialization: Artifacts contain stringified response objects instead of TextPart content
body:
### What happened?

The A2A SDK has a critical serialization bug where TextPart.text content is not properly extracted during transport. Instead of receiving the actual text content, clients receive the stringified representation of the entire response object containing artifacts.

# Expected Behavior

  1. Agent creates JSON content: `json_content = structured_response.model_dump_json()`
  2. Agent wraps in TextPart: `TextPart(text=json_content)`
  3. Agent adds to artifact: `Part(root=TextPart(text=json_content))`
  4. Client receives: The original json_content string

# Actual Behavior

  1. Agent creates JSON content: `json_content = structured_response.model_dump_json()` ✅
  2. Agent wraps in TextPart: `TextPart(text=json_content)` ✅
  3. Agent adds to artifact: `Part(root=TextPart(text=json_content))` ✅
  4. Client receives: `artifacts=[Artifact(artifact_id='...', description=None, extensions=None, metadata=None, name='consensus_analysis_result', parts=[Part(root=TextPart(kind='text', metad...`

# Evidence

The received content shows Python's default string representation of a list containing Artifact objects, not the intended JSON content.

  Debug output from client:

```
  DEBUG: Found 1 artifacts
  DEBUG: Artifact 0: has parts = True
  DEBUG: Artifact 0 has 1 parts
  DEBUG: Part 0: has root = True, root type = <class 'a2a.types.TextPart'>
  DEBUG: Found text content: artifacts=[Artifact(artifact_id='91f810b7-a027-40d9-9ad5-36d5dbce09f1', description=None, extensions...
```

# Environment

  - A2A SDK Version: `a2a-sdk==0.3.0`
  - Python Version: `3.13`
  - Transport: `JsonRpcTransport`
  - Setup: Docker containers with leader/follower agents

# Reproduction Steps

  1. Create an agent that generates structured JSON content
  2. Wrap content in TextPart(text=json_content)
  3. Add to artifact via `updater.add_artifact([Part(root=TextPart(text=content))])`
  4. Send through A2A transport to client
  5. Client extracts `part.root.text` - receives artifact structure instead of original content

# Minimal Reproduction Code

  Agent (sender):

```python
  # Generate structured content
  json_content = {"title": "Test", "data": "content"}
  json_string = json.dumps(json_content)

  # Create artifact with TextPart
  await updater.add_artifact(
      [Part(root=TextPart(text=json_string))],
      name="test_result"
  )
```

  Client (receiver):

```python
  # Extract content from artifact
  for artifact in response.artifacts:
      for part in artifact.parts:
          if hasattr(part, 'root') and hasattr(part.root, 'text'):
              content = part.root.text
              print(f"Received: {content}")
              # Expected: '{"title": "Test", "data": "content"}'
              # Actual: 'artifacts=[Artifact(artifact_id=...'
```

# Impact

  - Severity: Critical
  - Scope: Any A2A system passing structured content through artifacts
  - Workaround: Complex pattern matching to extract JSON from corrupted strings
  - Affects: Content extraction, structured data exchange, API responses

# Root Cause Analysis

The bug appears to be in the A2A transport/serialization layer where:

  1. The entire response object gets converted to string using Python's `str()` method
  2. Instead of extracting `TextPart.text` content during serialization
  3. This happens between agent artifact creation and client reception
  4. Likely in `JsonRpcTransport` or related serialization components

# Proposed Fix

The serialization layer should extract `TextPart.text` content rather than stringifying the entire response object. The transport mechanism needs to:

  1. Properly traverse the artifact structure
  2. Extract text content from `TextPart` objects
  3. Preserve the original text content during transport
  4. Ensure clients receive the intended content, not object representations

  Workaround Implemented

  We've implemented client-side detection and recovery:

```python
  def extract_json_from_corrupted_artifact(corrupted_content: str) -> str:
      """Extract actual JSON from A2A serialization bug artifacts."""
      # Pattern matching to recover JSON from artifact structure strings
      # Multiple fallback strategies for different corruption patterns
```

This workaround allows systems to function despite the bug, but the SDK should be fixed to prevent the corruption from occurring.

### Relevant log output

```shell
Debug output from client:

  DEBUG: Artifact 0: has parts = True
  DEBUG: Artifact 0 has 1 parts
  DEBUG: Part 0: has root = True, root type = <class 'a2a.types.TextPart'>
  DEBUG: Found text content: artifacts=[Artifact(artifact_id='91f810b7-a027-40d9-9ad5-36d5dbce09f1', description=None, extensions...
```

title: Gemini 2.5 Pro throws 400 Bad Request for any prompt due to url.format validation — works fine with GPT-4 (Goose v1.1.4)
body: Describe the bug When using the Gemini 2.5 Pro model in Goose (v1.1.4 on Windows), I receive the following error on every single prompt, even basic ones like "Hi" or "Hello": pgsql Copy Edit Request failed: Request failed with status: 400 Bad Request. Message: * GenerateContentRequest.tools[0].function_declarations[20].parameters.properties[url].format: only 'enum' and 'date-time' are supported for STRING type This issue does not occur when using GPT-4 or other OpenAI models with the same prompt and extension configuration. The error appears to originate from a tool/function being registered with a parameter named url using an invalid format. To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: Use Goose v1.1.4 on Windows Enable extensions: Computer Controller, Developer, Fetch, Pdfreader, Tutorial, and Memory (see screenshot) Select Gemini 2.5 Pro as provider/model Type any prompt (e.g., "Hi") Observe error: 400 Bad Request with message related to .parameters.properties[url].format Expected behavior Prompt should be processed normally. The Gemini model should return a response without error, as it does in other apps or via direct API access. Screenshots Error message screenshot Enabled extensions screenshot Please provide following information: OS & Arch: Windows 11 x64 Interface: UI Version: Goose v1.1.4 Extensions enabled: Computer Controller, Developer, Fetch, Pdfreader, Tutorial, Memory Provider & Model: Google - gemini-2.5-pro Other provider tested: OpenAI - gpt-4 (✅ works fine) Additional context This appears to be a schema validation issue specific to Gemini 2.5, which enforces stricter rules for function/tool parameters. It seems Goose or one of the enabled extensions is registering a tool with a parameter that includes: "url": { "type": "string", "format": "url" // ❌ not allowed by Gemini 2.5 } Only format: "enum" or format: "date-time" are supported on string types by Gemini. This needs to be stripped or replaced to ensure compatibility. Please advise on a fix or patch. Happy to help test or dig deeper if needed.

title: sub_recipe task should escape command parameter for correct yaml syntax.
body:
**Describe the bug**

I am trying the recipe workflow.

- main.yaml: the main recipe that has two sub recipe.
- news.yaml: sub recipe for fetching news with perplexity api.
- analyze.yaml: sub recipe to analyze the news.

The steps is:

  1. Call the fetch_news sub-recipe tool to get raw news data
  2. Pass the raw news data to the analyze sub-recipe tool
  3. Collect the prediction results from the analysis

The workflow fails at 2, when pass the raw news data to the analyze sub recipe tool, with error `Unsupported format`, see [source code](https://github.com/block/goose/blob/ba02ed906e5d7fbeb41092493390a2fabbf58f27/crates/goose/src/recipe/mod.rs#L304).

The reason I believe is because the raw data is markdown format, and the sub task request payload is yaml format, so the request is like this:

```
─── execute_task | sub_recipe ──────────────────────────
tasks:
    -
        id: 81c4f578-c642-43b5-af51-5deab1ecb319
        payload:
            sub_recipe:
                command_parameters:
                    raw_data: string with markdown format
                name: analyze
                recipe_path: recipes/analyze.yaml
        task_type: sub_recipe
```

Since the value of raw_data is markdown string, causing this payload become invalid yaml.

**To Reproduce**

- Create 3 recipe file, the main recipe should instruct the correct workflow as described  above.
- news sub recipe should be instructed to output markdown content.
- anaylze recipe should be able to recieve the raw_data parameter.

The pipeline workflow should work.

title: [Feature]: Add Amazon Bedrock Provider Support, Azure Streaming, and Flexible Client Configuration
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, the gollm implementation lacks support for Amazon Bedrock as a provider, which limits its applicability in AWS-native environments. Additionally, client configuration is tightly coupled to environment variables, reducing flexibility. Streaming support for Azure OpenAI is also unclear or absent.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Amazon Bedrock Support: Add a bedrock provider implementation that conforms to the gollm.Client interface, supporting both Claude and Amazon models via the Bedrock runtime API.

Client Configuration Flexibility: Allow overriding environment-based defaults (e.g., api_key, base_url, model) using the ClientOptions struct when instantiating a client.

Azure OpenAI Streaming: Add streaming support to the Azure OpenAI provider similar to how openai.Chat supports streaming via CreateChatCompletionStream.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using OpenAI/Ollama providers only, but this excludes AWS-native deployments and limits integration into Bedrock-secured environments.

Manually modifying the provider code to inject custom configs, but this is brittle and doesn’t scale.

Forking the repo to build streaming separately for Azure, though this would diverge from the core project unnecessarily.

**Additional context**
I'd be happy to contribute the Bedrock provider implementation, and optionally assist with Azure streaming support and client configuration refactor. If there's interest, I can follow up with a PR after discussion.

Thanks!
—Augustin

## Goal
Enhance Genie's learning framework to support comprehensive context accumulation and structured insight extraction.

Based on analysis of advanced context engineering patterns that show:
- Comprehensive contexts > compressed summaries for LLM performance
- Separation of reflection (insight extraction) from curation improves quality
- Incremental delta updates prevent context collapse

## Multi-Phase Implementation

## 🎯 Major Features

### 1. 🏗️ Install Architecture Redesign (Latest)

**Problem:** 2-step install flow (CLI explore → Master install) was complex and used CODE_EXPLORE incorrectly.

**Solution:** 1-step orchestration where Master Genie handles everything.

**Architecture:**
```
Before: CLI → Explore (extract context) → Master (with context)
After:  CLI → Master → Master orchestrates (explore → interview → spawn installers)
```

**Key Changes:**
- ✅ EXPLORE is now a global agent (not CODE_EXPLORE) 
- ✅ Master receives simple prompt: "Run explorer to acquire context, when it ends run the install workflow"
- ✅ Code + Create installers run IN PARALLEL (users can interact with both simultaneously)
- ✅ Simplified CLI: 4 functions deleted, 1 entry point added
- ✅ Clear file ownership: Code creates tech files, Create creates product files
- ✅ Create expansion awareness: Users know Create can generate spells/agents on-demand

**Files Modified:**

### 2. 🧠 Learning System Phase 3 - Structured Bullets

**Problem:** Unstructured narrative learnings hard to retrieve, measure, and deduplicate.

**Solution:** Convert all learnings to structured bullets with unique IDs.

**Scale:**
- ✅ Converted **~800+ learnings** across **17 core spells**
- ✅ Added bullet-id generator, bullet-counter, bullet-find tools

**Spells Converted:**
- `learn.md` (73 learnings)

### 3. 🔍 Semantic Deduplication System

**Problem:** Manual deduplication ineffective, context bloat from similar learnings.

**Solution:** Local embeddings helper for semantic similarity detection.

**Architecture:**

title: 🐛 Agent sync deletes user neuron prompts
body:
## Problem

Running `genie init` or `genie update` **deletes user-created neuron prompts** in `.genie/neurons/` directory.

## Root Cause

The `neurons/` directory is **NOT in the template sync blacklist**, so user neuron files are deleted when syncing templates.

## Current Blacklist (paths.ts:99-109)

```typescript
export function getTemplateRelativeBlacklist(): Set<string> {
  return new Set([
    'cli',        // Framework code
    'mcp',        // Framework code
    'backups',    // User backups ✓
    'wishes',     // User wishes ✓
    'reports',    // User reports ✓
    'state'       // User session state ✓
    // 'neurons' ❌ MISSING!
  ]);
}
```

## The Fix (1 Line)

**File: `.genie/cli/src/lib/paths.ts` line 109**

```typescript
export function getTemplateRelativeBlacklist(): Set<string> {
  return new Set([
    'cli',
    'mcp',
    'backups',
    'wishes',
    'reports',
    'state',
    'neurons'  // ← ADD THIS LINE
  ]);
}
```

## User Impact Evidence

Users have documented permanent neuron architecture with custom naming patterns:

**File: `.genie/wishes/wish-120-a-forge-drop-in-replacement/reports/LEARNING-PERMANENT-NEURONS-20251018.md`**

Legitimate user-created files being destroyed during sync:
- Custom agent configurations
- Neuron prompt variations
- User-specific orchestration patterns

## How It Happens

1. User creates custom neuron in `.genie/neurons/my-custom-neuron.md`
2. User runs `genie update` (or re-runs `genie init`)
3. `copyTemplateFiles()` is called (init.ts:379-415)
4. Uses blacklist from `getTemplateRelativeBlacklist()`
5. `neurons/` is NOT blacklisted
6. Template sync overwrites/deletes user's custom neurons
7. User loses custom work

## Protection Status

| Directory | Protected? | Why |
|-----------|------------|-----|
| `cli/` | ✓ | Framework code |
| `mcp/` | ✓ | Framework code |
| `backups/` | ✓ | User data |
| `wishes/` | ✓ | User data |
| `reports/` | ✓ | User data |
| `state/` | ✓ | User data |
| **`neurons/`** | **✗** | **BUG** |

## Testing Procedure

1. Create test neuron: `.genie/neurons/test-custom-neuron.md`
2. Run `genie init` (in existing workspace)
3. Verify `test-custom-neuron.md` still exists
4. Run `genie update`
5. Verify `test-custom-neuron.md` still exists

- `/home/namastex/workspace/automagik-genie/.genie/cli/src/lib/paths.ts` (lines 99-109) - FIX HERE
- `/home/namastex/workspace/automagik-genie/.genie/cli/src/commands/init.ts` (lines 379-415) - Uses blacklist
- `/home/namastex/workspace/automagik-genie/.genie/cli/src/lib/fs-utils.ts` (lines 18-32) - copyDirectory implementation

body: ## Bug Description User was getting schema validation errors using search_notes tool with ChatGPT > But this is from the docs, "entity" is note type and not observation category ``` Filter by observation category: python Find all decisions decisions = await search_notes( query="", entity_types=["decision"], project="main" ) Find problems and solutions issues = await search_notes( query="performance", entity_types=["problem", "solution"], project="main" ) ``` It's failing whatever I try Request { query: training, project: Training Management, page_size: 10, entity_types: [\"problem\"] } Response Input validation error: '["problem"]' is not valid under any of the given schemas I've tried to force it to use 'entity' as well as variations of the search term structure (strings, array, ...) Correct. Try “type” instead of entity_type. Entity type should either be “entity” “observation” The type will query the frontmatter “type” value. Which is what you are probably after. luck.exe — 6:16 PM Okay, now I'm confused too. Sorry. I want it to search for [observation] categories, e.g., the category [requirement] and not for note types (set in the YAML front matter) search_notes("Training Management", "[requirement]", entity_types=["observation"]) That should be working? ## Environment - ChatGPT bug fix ``` Bug Analysis The MCP tool signature still annotates types and entity_types as Optional[List[str]], so the generated JSON schema insists on an actual array value (repo/src/basic_memory/mcp/tools/search.py:208 and repo/src/basic_memory/mcp/tools/search.py:209). Clients like Claude Desktop therefore reject JSON-stringified arrays during pre-validation, yielding the reported '["observation"]' is not valid under any of the given schemas message before the request ever reaches our server. On the server side we do try to be permissive: FastMCP’s argument handling will JSON-decode strings into native lists if it ever sees them (repo/.venv/Lib/site-packages/mcp/server/fastmcp/utilities/func_metadata.py:121), so the business logic actually tolerates either format once validation passes. Integration tests only exercise the success path where the client provides a real list (repo/test-int/mcp/test_search_integration.py:329), so this schema mismatch slipped through and our docs that say “use JSON format” end up guiding Claude users into a shape the schema disallows. Fix Plan Broaden the tool parameter schema so it explicitly allows both a string (that we’ll JSON-decode) and a list for types/entity_types, then normalize inside search_notes before building the SearchQuery. Mirror the change for both filters to keep behaviour consistent. Add regression coverage that calls search_notes through the MCP surface with JSON-string parameters to confirm the FastMCP parsing path works once the schema accepts the input. Refresh user-facing docs/examples to clarify: Preferred shape is a real list when the client supports it. JSON-string form is accepted for clients that can only send text payloads. Note the same guidance for the types filter so both stay aligned. Right now Claude Desktop (or any client that serializes tool parameters as strings inside XML) can’t get a filtered search through—the tool schema only accepts a real JSON array for entity_types, so validation fails before the request ever hits the Basic Memory server (repo/src/basic_memory/mcp/tools/search.py:208). Claude’s XML wrapper turns ["observation"] into a literal string, which is rejected. The only searches that succeed today are the unfiltered ones (omit entity_types/types) or queries that encode the filter in the text itself—e.g. category:observation—which piggyback on the search syntax instead of the structured parameters. Until the schema is made more permissive (as in the plan I shared), Claude can’t send a structured filter that reaches the server. ```

linked_prs.title: Move to 'Azure.Identity' v1.14.2 and refactor the telemetry library
linked_prs.body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

## PR Summary

Fix #393

I can reproduce this issue on macOS with the error from `AzurePowerShellCredential()` being `"PowerShell did not return a valid response."` This turns out to be an issue with the `Azure.Identity` library (https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues/50578). After moving to the latest `1.14.2` of the package, it works for me on macOS.

----

However, moving to the `1.14.2` of the `Azure.Identity` caused a dependency conflict with the `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.WorkerService` package, which brings in an older version of `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` that conflicts with the newer version of `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions` that comes with `Azure.Identity`.

In fact, we should not depend on `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.WorkerService`, but instead should use `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights` directly. The `WorkerService` package was designed for ASP.NET Core applications that need automatic dependency injection, performance counters, and various auto-collectors. For a simple console application that just needs to send traces and exceptions to Application Insights, the core `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights` package is perfect and much more appropriate.

**What were changed:** (summarized by GitHub Copilot)

- Replaced `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.WorkerService` with just `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights`
- Simplified the telemetry initialization from a complex DI setup to a simple direct instantiation
- Used modern `TelemetryConfiguration.CreateDefault()` with connection string instead of deprecated approaches

**Benefits of the change:** (summarized by GitHub Copilot)

- Dramatically reduced dependencies - We went from 67+ transitive packages to about 25
- Eliminated version conflicts - No more conflicting DI framework versions
- Simpler code - The constructor is now much cleaner and easier to understand
- Faster build times - Fewer packages to restore and compile
- Smaller deployment - Much lighter runtime footprint
- Same functionality - You still get exactly the same telemetry capabilities

title: Prompt Profiles
body:
### Duplicates

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Summary 💡
Based on previous comments: https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT/issues/3858#issuecomment-1537439701

- We have roughly 10+ open PRs that are all about augmenting/replacing hard-coded prompts. 
- Many of these cannot be committed due to the lack of testing/benchmarks
- However, this causes a ton of potentially useful contributions to end up in the backlog

Thus, the idea is to add support for so called "Prompt Profiles". A profile would be the equivalent of a sub-directory that contains a single profiles.json file to list sub-directories with other prompt configs.

Given that prompt-related PRs are such a common thing but due to the lack of testing data also are so controversial, how about coming up with support for "prompt profiles", as in a shared folder with sub-folders that contain profiles for different prompts, so that people can tinker with different profiles without stepping on anyone's toes ?

This will enable people to experiment with different "prompt profiles", without affecting the stability/usefulness of the whole project. Also, this would present an option to benchmark (#1359) different prompft profiles against each other (#1354). So, if/when a prompt is promoted to become the official/main one, we can simply change a "default_profile" property.

Having this sort of infrastructure in place would also provide a good baseline for regression testing and benchmarking.
It would not directly be the solution proposed in https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT/issues/3858, but probably would be the only solution to have our cake and eat it, while also growing test data ?

Ideally we'd support a dedicated sub-folder for "prompt profiles" with the corresponding json to map directories to each profile - that way, we can have our cake and eat it, and still close 10+ PRs in the process, because these would then all become custom prompt profiles - without any chance to step on anyone's toe. Besides, this would also mean having 10+ different ways to benchmark/test the system in conjunction with different prompts EASILY

title: [BUG] entity_type usage is unclear and conflicting between tools
body:
That is confusing. Sorry, we should make the docs more clear. 

Basic Memory has three basic Entities (entity_types): Entity (a note), Observation (a fact in a note), Relation (connection. between Entities)

the "type" is also a property in the frontmatter. 

```
---
title: Document Title
type: note
tags: [tag1, tag2]
permalink: custom-path
---

# Document Title
Regular markdown content...

## Observations
- [category] Content with #tags (optional context)

## Relations
- relation_type [[Other Document]] (optional context)
```

## write note

# Create a note with tags and entity type
        write_note(
            project="work-project",
            title="API Design",
            folder="specs",
            content="# REST API Specification\\n\\n- implements [[Authentication]]",
            tags=["api", "design"],
            entity_type="guide"
        )
The "entity_type" arg here refers to the value in the frontmatter. 

## search

Admittedly, it's inconsistent:
 
    - `search_notes("work-docs", "query", types=["note", "person"])` - Multiple content types
    - `search_notes("research", "query", entity_types=["observation"])` - Filter by entity type
    - `search_notes("team-docs", "query", after_date="2024-01-01")` - Recent content only
    - `search_notes("my-project", "query", after_date="1 week")` - Relative date filtering

the "types" refers to the frontmatter value. The "entity_types" refers to the type of Entity.

## Action

We should use the "entity_type" definition consistently, or preferably use a arg clearer name: "note_type" for write note.

linked_prs.title: fix: Rename write_note entity_type to note_type for clarity
linked_prs.body:
Resolves #403

This PR addresses the confusing parameter naming between `write_note` and `search_notes` tools.

## Problem
The `entity_type` parameter in `write_note` sets the frontmatter type field, while `entity_types` in `search_notes` filters by database Entity/Observation/Relation types. This inconsistency created confusion for users.

## Solution
Rename `entity_type` → `note_type` in `write_note` to make it clear this parameter sets the note's frontmatter type, not the database entity type.

## Changes
- Renamed parameter in `src/basic_memory/mcp/tools/write_note.py`
- Updated parameter documentation with clearer description
- Updated all examples in `docs/ai-assistant-guide-extended.md`
- Updated all test cases in `tests/mcp/test_tool_write_note.py`
- Internal Entity schema field remains `entity_type` (no breaking change)

## Testing
- All existing write_note tests updated to use new parameter name
- No changes to internal API or database schema


Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

title: feat: multi model and multi provider config and auto switching (lead/worker consolidation/simplification)
body:
WIP PR: https://github.com/block/goose/pull/4035 starting with just the mechanism, as there are other changes to unify the config I don't wnat to get in the way of Need to be able to configure multiple models and providers for different purposes, and untangle lead/worker config and code. ### Discussed in https://github.com/block/goose/discussions/3980
Originally posted by **michaelneale** August 9, 2025 I started looking at how we can consolidate things around lead/worker and provider config (vs env vars), lead worker is currently special cased (and wont' support streaming for example), and uses environment variables, a whole variety of confusing things. What we could do is have a more general config something like: ```yaml models: - provider: grok model: grok4 purpose: oracle - provider: openai model: gpt-5 purpose: second-opinion - provider: anthropic model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514 purpose: worker - provider: anthropic model: claude-opus-4-20250514 purpose: lead ``` where there are multiple providers configured for different purposes. Lead/worker is just one case (it could have just one by default, similar to before). oracle is for one of consultation, second-opinion for when assistance is needed and so on (can add extra metadata to help the routing/gating decisions, but don't want to get bogged in that detail). This would also go along with simplifying the lead/worker code to be less of a special case, and more about tracking what provider is in use and switching, and loading config from one place ideally (and not only rely on environment variables). While making that change, this can also use a simpler config format (of course for compat/command line etc - can still have env vars set when that isn't used)

linked_prs.title: feat: multi model and multi provider config and auto switching
linked_prs.body:
This generalises the GOOSE_LEAD/WORKER variable structure with a more general multi model approach (ie can remove that old code path). 
This is clearly marked with an x- experimental config prefix (as per convention) so the exact format can evolve as people use this. 

This is really phase 1, phase 2 will be both GUI/ux changes to support and also having more opionionated defaults when providers are configured, but need to get this out in the wild so we can see how things perform with all the permutations of providers we can't test by hand.

For example, in config: 

```yaml
x-advanced-models:
- provider: databricks
  model: goose-gpt-5
  role: reviewer
- provider: anthropic
  model: claude-opus-4-1-20250805
  role: deep-thinker
- provider: anthropic
  model: claude-opus-4-1-20250805
  role: lead
```

which maps to `premade_roles.yaml` which define rules for those models and when they activate: 

```yaml
roles:
  # Deep reasoning and analysis
  - role: "deep-thinker"
    rules:
      triggers:
        keywords: ["think", "reason", "analyze", "explain why", "how does", "what if"]
        match_type: "any"
        complexity_threshold: "high"
        source: "human"  # Only trigger on human messages
      active_turns: 3
      priority: 10
```

which can be used as is - or each trigger value/setting can be overridding in the personal config (if one of the pre-made set doesn't fit - normally you just say role + provider + model - and let it work it out, but you can customise). 

By default the main provider/model is used, and these will supplement when the rules are activate/met, and run for a certain amount of time (this already helped me as the gptoss:120B model was good at spotting short circuit logic bugs other models failed to see). 

This could also be used to do most of the work in a low cost or zero cost local model as well.

run with `--debug` to see it log switching providers and models as it works




discussion https://github.com/block/goose/discussions/3980 
implements: https://github.com/block/goose/issues/4036

Yes.  
This issue concerns configuring and switching between multiple LLM providers and models for different agent roles (lead/worker), which directly relates to agent-specific behaviors, provider integration, and workflow orchestration—core aspects of agent issues per the taxonomy.

title: Bug: MCP genie:run selects wrong executor profile (DEFAULT instead of agent-specific)
body:
## Summary
When using `mcp__genie__run` to start an agent session, the executor profile selection falls back to `DEFAULT` variant instead of using the agent-specific profile (e.g., `explore` agent should use `EXPLORE` variant).

## Impact
- **Medium:** Agent runs with generic `DEFAULT` profile instead of optimized agent-specific profile
- **Medium:** May use incorrect model or configuration for the agent's intended purpose
- **Low:** Affects agent performance and specialization

## Environment
- **Genie version:** 2.5.8-rc.1
- **Trigger:** `mcp__genie__run(agent="explore", prompt="...")`
- **Expected:** `executor=CLAUDE_CODE/EXPLORE`
- **Actual:** `executor=CLAUDE_CODE/DEFAULT`

## Root Cause

**Files:**
- `.genie/cli/src/cli-core/handlers/run.ts:147-194` (executor resolution logic)
- `.genie/code/agents/explore.md` (missing executor profile metadata)

The executor profile resolution follows this order:
1. Agent frontmatter (`genie.executorProfile` or `genie.executorVariant`)
2. Config defaults (`config.defaults.executorVariant`)
3. Fallback to `DEFAULT`

The `explore` agent doesn't specify an executor profile in its frontmatter, so resolution falls back to config defaults.

## Evidence

MCP tool output:
\`\`\`
mcp__genie__run(agent="explore", prompt="...")
→ Started code/explore in background (executor=CLAUDE_CODE/DEFAULT, model=sonnet)
                                                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ WRONG
\`\`\`

Expected:
\`\`\`
→ Started code/explore in background (executor=CLAUDE_CODE/EXPLORE, model=sonnet)
                                                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ CORRECT
\`\`\`

## Proposed Fixes

### Option 1: Add Executor Metadata to Agent (Recommended)

Update `.genie/code/agents/explore.md` frontmatter:

\`\`\`yaml
---
name: explore
description: Discovery-focused exploratory reasoning
genie:
  executor: CLAUDE_CODE
  executorProfile: EXPLORE  # or executorVariant: EXPLORE
  model: sonnet  # optional: specify model if needed
---
\`\`\`

**Pros:**
- Explicit configuration per agent
- Easy to maintain and audit
- Follows existing pattern

**Cons:**
- Requires updating every agent file

### Option 2: Add Profile Inference Logic

Update `resolveExecutionSelection()` in `run.ts`:

\`\`\`typescript
function resolveExecutionSelection(
  config: HandlerContext['config'],
  parsed: ParsedCommand,
  agentGenie: Record<string, any>,
  agentName: string  // Add agent name parameter
): { executorKey: string; executorVariant: string; model?: string; modeName: string } {
  // ... existing code ...

  // Infer variant from agent name if not explicitly set
  if (!variant || variant === 'DEFAULT') {
    const knownVariants = ['explore', 'implement', 'review', 'debug', 'fix', 'test'];
    const agentNameLower = agentName.toLowerCase();
    
    // Check if agent name matches a known variant
    for (const known of knownVariants) {
      if (agentNameLower.includes(known)) {
        variant = known.toUpperCase();
        break;
      }
    }
  }

  // ... rest of code ...
}
\`\`\`

**Pros:**
- Works for all agents automatically
- No manual configuration needed
- Convention over configuration

**Cons:**
- Implicit behavior (less obvious)
- May incorrectly infer for agents with ambiguous names

### Option 3: Hybrid Approach (Best)

1. Add profile inference as fallback (Option 2)
2. Allow explicit override via frontmatter (Option 1)
3. Resolution order:
   - Agent frontmatter (`executorProfile`)
   - Inferred from agent name
   - Config defaults
   - `DEFAULT`

## Reproduction Steps

1. Start MCP server: `genie mcp -t stdio`
2. From Claude Desktop or MCP client:
   \`\`\`
   mcp__genie__run(agent="explore", prompt="test")
   \`\`\`
3. Observe output: `executor=CLAUDE_CODE/DEFAULT` ❌
4. Expected: `executor=CLAUDE_CODE/EXPLORE` ✅

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Agent `explore` uses `CLAUDE_CODE/EXPLORE` profile
- [ ] Other agents (implement, review, debug, etc.) use correct profiles
- [ ] Profile resolution checks agent metadata before defaulting
- [ ] Add test: verify executor profile selection for known agents
- [ ] Document executor profile resolution order

## Related Files

- `.genie/cli/src/cli-core/handlers/run.ts` (lines 147-194)
- `.genie/cli/src/lib/forge-executor.ts` (lines 510-530)
- `.genie/mcp/src/server.ts` (lines 217-270)
- `.genie/code/agents/explore.md` (frontmatter)
- `.genie/code/agents/implementor.md` (example with profile)
- `.genie/code/agents/review.md` (example with profile)

## Priority

**Medium** - Affects execution quality but not blocking

```bash
# OpenCUA — End-to-end Agent
```

linked_prs.title: Add starred repository support to GitHub MCP server
linked_prs.body:
This PR implements comprehensive starred repository functionality for the GitHub MCP server, addressing the feature request to enable agents to search and manage starred repositories.

Also removes the github-mcp-server binary, which prob was accidentally commited.

## What's Added

### New Tools

**`list_starred_repositories`** - Lists starred repositories for the authenticated user or a specified user
- Optional `username` parameter to list starred repos for any user
- Sorting options by `created` (when starred) or `updated` (when repo was last pushed)
- Standard pagination support
- Returns repositories in `MinimalRepository` format with additional `starred_at` field

**`star_repository`** - Stars a repository
- Requires `owner` and `repo` parameters
- Returns success confirmation message

**`unstar_repository`** - Unstars a repository  
- Requires `owner` and `repo` parameters
- Returns success confirmation message

### Implementation Details

- All tools follow existing patterns and use the same error handling approach
- Added `starred_at` field to `MinimalRepository` struct to track when repositories were starred 🔴 
- Tools are registered in the `repos` toolset (read-only for listing, write tools for starring/unstarring)
- Comprehensive test coverage with mocked HTTP clients following existing test patterns
- Updated README documentation with complete parameter descriptions

## Use Cases

This enables powerful agent workflows like:

```
"Show me my starred Python projects that have been updated recently"
"Star the facebook/react repository for future reference"
"List repositories that @transitive-bullshit has starred, sorted by star count"
"Find my starred machine learning repositories with more than 1000 stars"
```

## API Coverage

Implements GitHub's starred repository REST API endpoints:
- `GET /user/starred` - List starred repositories for authenticated user
- `GET /users/{username}/starred` - List starred repositories for specific user
- `PUT /user/starred/{owner}/{repo}` - Star a repository
- `DELETE /user/starred/{owner}/{repo}` - Unstar a repository

The implementation enables agents to leverage users' curated collections of starred repositories as a high-quality signal for dependency selection and project discovery, as mentioned in the original issue.

title: [Feature] Token-efficient AI-to-AI orchestration output modes
body:
## Problem

The Genie CLI was originally designed for human consumption with rich, verbose outputs. It's now used for AI-to-AI orchestration (main Genie orchestrating subagent neurons), but the verbose output format causes token explosion.

**Current cost:**
- Single session view: ~16k tokens (804 lines)
- Orchestrating 3-4 subagents: 36-48k tokens just for monitoring (18-24% of budget!)
- Forces premature context trimming
- Limits complex multi-agent orchestration patterns

## Solution: Architectural Simplification

Replace the current 4-layer rendering pipeline with a direct 2-layer markdown pipeline.

### Current Architecture (4 layers of overhead)

```
1. Executors emit JSONL events
   ↓ (stored in log files)
2. Log viewers parse JSONL → ChatMessage[]
   ↓ (.genie/cli/src/executors/*-log-viewer.ts)
3. View builders create ViewEnvelope tree
   ↓ (.genie/cli/src/views/*.ts)
4. Ink renderer → React components → terminal ANSI
   ↓ (.genie/cli/src/view/render.tsx - 560 lines)
   Terminal output (verbose, 16k tokens)
```

**Layers 3-4 are heavyweight overhead:**
- ViewEnvelope/ViewNode tree construction
- Ink (React for CLIs) rendering with component hierarchy
- Complex ANSI escape code generation
- No token efficiency consideration

### Proposed Architecture (2 layers, clean)

```
1. Executors emit JSONL events
   ↓ (stored in log files)  
2. Log viewers parse JSONL → ChatMessage[]
   ↓ (.genie/cli/src/executors/transcript-utils.ts)
   [NEW] Markdown formatter → compact markdown
   ↓
   Output (markdown by default, optional json/html)
```

**Key insight:** We already have structured `ChatMessage[]` data with role, title, and body. Just need to format it as compact markdown instead of building a React component tree.

### Why Markdown-Only

- ✅ Works for both humans and AI
- ✅ Can be rendered in UI later if needed
- ✅ Simpler implementation (no mode detection)
- ✅ Consistent format across all consumers
- ✅ Future-proof for rendering
- ✅ 96-98% token reduction

### Three Output Modes

1. **'final'** (completed tasks) → Only last message (mini-report), no wrapper
2. **'recent'** (in-progress, default) → Latest 5 messages, compact markdown
3. **'overview'** (full:true) → Session metadata + checkpoints + state

**Token targets:**
- Completed tasks: 16k → 0.5k (96% reduction)
- In-progress monitoring: 16k → 0.3k (98% reduction)
- Session overviews: 16k → 0.4k (97% reduction)

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Markdown Formatter (NEW)
**Create:** `.genie/cli/src/lib/markdown-formatter.ts` (~150 lines)

**Functions:**
- `formatTranscriptMarkdown(messages: ChatMessage[], meta, mode): string`
  - Formats session transcripts with 3 modes
  - Includes metadata (tokens, tool calls, model)
  - Token budget limits (max 500 tokens per response)
- `formatSessionListMarkdown(sessions): string`
  - Formats session overview tables
  - Compact single-line per session
- `formatMetadata(metrics): string`
  - Formats header metadata compactly

**No changes to:**
- JSONL event parsing (transcript-utils.ts)
- ChatMessage[] structure
- Executor implementations

### Phase 2: Replace View Layer
**Modify:**
- `.genie/cli/src/commands/view.ts` - Use markdown formatter instead of buildChatView
- `.genie/cli/src/commands/list.ts` - Use markdown formatter instead of buildRunsOverviewView

**Keep:**
- JSON output mode (already exists at render.tsx:45-49)
- Optional HTML output (future enhancement)

### Phase 3: Remove Ink Rendering
**Delete:**
- `.genie/cli/src/view/render.tsx` (560 lines of Ink/React rendering)
- `.genie/cli/src/views/chat.ts` (buildChatView, ViewEnvelope construction)
- `.genie/cli/src/views/runs.ts` (buildRunsOverviewView)
- ViewEnvelope/ViewNode type definitions

**Keep:**
- `.genie/cli/src/lib/executor-prompt.tsx` (interactive executor selection - still uses Ink)

### Phase 4: MCP Integration
**Modify:**
- `.genie/cli/src/cli-core/handlers/view.ts` (or wherever MCP view is handled)
- MCP server returns compact markdown directly (currently wraps in ViewEnvelope)
- Enables efficient AI-to-AI orchestration

## Files Affected

**Remove entirely:**
- `.genie/cli/src/view/render.tsx` (Ink rendering, 560 lines)
- `.genie/cli/src/views/chat.ts` (ViewEnvelope builders)
- `.genie/cli/src/views/runs.ts` (session list builders)
- ViewEnvelope/ViewNode abstractions (view-model.ts types)

**Add new:**
- `.genie/cli/src/lib/markdown-formatter.ts` (~150 lines)

**Modify:**
- Command handlers (view, list) to use markdown formatter
- MCP response formatting

**Keep unchanged:**
- `.genie/cli/src/executors/transcript-utils.ts` (JSONL → ChatMessage[] parsing)
- `.genie/cli/src/executors/claude-log-viewer.ts` (conversation parsing)
- `.genie/cli/src/executors/codex-log-viewer.ts` (metrics extraction)
- `.genie/cli/src/lib/executor-prompt.tsx` (interactive selector still uses Ink)
- ChatMessage[] structure
- Session storage

**Current Ink usage (only 2 files):**
- `.genie/cli/src/view/render.tsx` ← DELETE
- `.genie/cli/src/lib/executor-prompt.tsx` ← KEEP

## Success Metrics

- ✅ Token savings: 96-98% for AI orchestration
- ✅ Overall orchestration cost: 36k → 1.5k tokens (for 3 subagents)
- ✅ Budget freed: ~17% for actual reasoning
- ✅ Information loss: <5%
- ✅ Backward compatible: existing workflows unchanged
- ✅ Simpler codebase: 2 layers instead of 4
- ✅ Faster rendering: no React/Ink overhead

## Use Cases

1. **Orchestrator monitoring** - Check subagent progress (400 tokens vs 16k)
2. **Completed task check** - Get final mini-report only (500 tokens vs 12k)
3. **Parallel orchestration** - Monitor 10+ subagents within budget (currently limited to 3-4)

## Migration Strategy

**Backward compatible:** Existing ChatMessage[] structure unchanged, so all parsing logic remains valid.

**Output format:** Markdown by default (simpler). Optional JSON/HTML modes for structured data or future UI needs.

**No breaking changes:** Commands work the same, just output format is more compact.

## Context

Discovered during natural-routing-skills wish execution when orchestrator neuron session views consumed excessive tokens. This blocks efficient multi-agent orchestration and limits Genie's ability to use specialist neurons effectively.

title: Google provider: JSON Schema 'const' in tool schemas causes Pydantic/Gemini errors
body:
Running with the Google provider fails because tool parameter schemas include JSON Schema 'const'. This triggers either Pydantic validation errors or a Gemini API 400.

To reproduce:
1) Run:
  ` uvx fast-agent-mcp go --model google.gemini-2.5-pro --uvx wcgw`
2) Type: hi

Observed errors
- Pydantic validation (before provider request):
  ValidationError: ... properties.*.const ... Extra inputs are not permitted

- Gemini API (after getting past Pydantic):
  Google API Error: 400
  Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "const" at ...parameters...

Environment
- OS: Linux (Fedora) x86_64
- Python: 3.13
- uv: 0.8.23
- fast-agent-mcp: latest via uvx
- Model: google.gemini-2.5-pro

Notes
- Offending places include fields like allowed_globs / allowed_commands that use const: "all".
- google.genai function_declarations don’t accept 'const'; Pydantic may also reject it.

Workaround verified locally
- In src/fast_agent/llm/provider/google/google_converter.py:
  - If const is a string, rewrite to enum: [value].
  - If const is non-string, drop the constraint to avoid Gemini 400.
- With this, the repro initializes and responds.

Proposal
- Update _clean_schema_for_google to rewrite/remove 'const' as above (and continue stripping other unsupported keys).

Yes.

Explanation:  
This issue involves tool parameter schemas, LLM provider integration (Google Gemini), and errors in tool invocation due to schema incompatibility. The proposed patch modifies agent-specific code handling LLM/tool schemas, fitting the "Tool-related issues" and "Incompatibility with LLM providers" agent issue categories.

title: Procedural Memory / Tool building
body:
### Duplicates

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Summary 💡

Mentioned on Discord: https://discord.com/channels/1092243196446249134/1100458518693281873/1100472662452600972

Obviously, AutoGPT can already build custom tools (scripts)  - however, it might make sense to formalize this:

The idea discussed on discord was to allow it to grow a library of tools - so that it can extend itself over time and reuse its own tools for different projects and purposes (which would imply that tools would not be workspace specific).

That sounds actually like a good idea to me - and it would help with the issue of workspaces lacking persistence and of agents not being able to suspend/resume currently.

This way, at least, created tools could be reused.

A straightforward step would be to add a new command "create_tool" that then takes some specs for the tool to build, and which will add the tool building process to a JSON file that lives outside the workspace. That way, the agent could reuse these tools for future work.

We could add a corresponding list_tools command that would then traverse the json file/tool directory to list all tools and treat them analogous to "commands", using the I/O specs previously defined.

So, basically the agent would get new commands to:

- list tools
- create_tool
- execute_tool 

This would not be doing much more than use create_script / execute_python respectively - except that it could go through a handful of steps that involve gathering data/specs and serializing those to some file on disk (think JSON).

Once a tool is finished, it would show up and could be used by agents for future tasks

Over time, this could be adapted to also take a "type" parameter, where type could be:

- standalone python script
- autogpt command
- autogpt plugin

This would cover most use-cases we've previously seen in #15, and it would be a first step towards self-improvement.



### Examples 🌈

An agent needing to scrape a website as part of its tasks should create a generic and reusable tool as part of a "tools workspace" where it may store stuff that could come in handy later on.
The main objective here being to save time/resources, and update a list of built-in tools that were previously created/tested and that are functional.

Future instances having to use similar tools could either use those, or -by looking at the code inside the "tools workspace"- come up with custom/adapted versions of the tool in question.
The idea would be to do recursive test-driven-development to adapt existing tools as needed. This may involve supporting versioning, so that new/adapted tools use a different version number.

Tools could by convention provide a query parameter to learn more about their capabilities - so that an ai agent could run a tool to learn more about it (think --help --verbose but for BIFs)

The tool builder would be provided with a template for building new tools, so that a certain struture is used by all tools. Tools would contain sufficient comments/docstrings to provide context for self-modification. And each functional part of a tool would be required to come with tests to ensure that a tool is functioning, but also to identify areas that are not yet functional - which could then be used by an agent to narrow down/focus itself to "finish" a tool.

### Motivation 🔦

autogpt tends to create a ton of scripts to accomplish its tasks - often, these are only useful to the very instance that originally created the script - other instances will usually not know how to use such tools, even if they encounter the corresponding scripts.

It would make sense for autogpt to specifically create tools with a focus on being able to reuse those, this entails encoding input/output requirements (parameters / return values) and the current state of a tool's development. 
Once a tool is "finished" it would show up in the library of tools.

It would be a first step towards autogpt being able to extend itself, i.e. to self-improve in a reusable fashion.
Without that being specific to a single agent/project [session].

We could prime the "tool builder" to focus on coming up with generic tools that may be of use in the future, and that may also be of use to others.

It is likely that this way ANY autogpt instance will at least partially work toward a common goal, so that future instances have less work to do, which will save time/resources (API tokens)

The development process could go through a handful of stages or levels:
- gathering specs (possibly by creating an .md file)
- coming up with a stub / filled with comments
- incrementally filling in the stubs
- coming up with unit tests for each part
- analyze/improve and optimize the code

For starters, the tool builder could get restriction for each associated file to be restricted to a size that fits the context window, e.g. to split up each "tool" into N python files that don't need more than ~3000 tokens. N could be made configurable. Which should improve the odds of the tool builder succeeding at its work.

title: RuntimeException: Unsupported finish reason "STOP" in ResultConverter (Gemini bridge)
body:
Describe the bug 🎯

When using the Symfony AI Platform with Gemini, a fatal error occurs if the model response contains the finish reason "STOP".

Instead of being handled gracefully, it triggers a RuntimeException:

PHP Fatal error: Uncaught Symfony\AI\Platform\Exception\RuntimeException: Unsupported finish reason "STOP".
in vendor/symfony/ai-platform/src/Bridge/Gemini/Gemini/ResultConverter.php:130

Expected behavior ✅
- No exception should be thrown in this case.

Actual behavior 🐛
- "STOP" is not supported in ResultConverter.
- This leads to a fatal error and crashes the application.

Steps to reproduce 🔄
- Call Gemini through the Symfony AI Platform with code_execution server tool enabled.
- Receive a response where finishReason = "STOP".
- The error occurs inside ResultConverter->convertChoice().

Error log 📋
```
Uncaught Symfony\AI\Platform\Exception\RuntimeException: Unsupported finish reason "STOP".
in vendor/symfony/ai-platform/src/Bridge/Gemini/Gemini/ResultConverter.php:130
Stack trace:
#0 ResultConverter->convertChoice()
#1 ResultConverter->convert()
#2 ResultPromise->await()
#3 Agent->call()
#4 Program->__invoke()
```

Environment 🌍
AI Platform version: latest (from main)
Gemini model: 2.5 Pro
PHP version: 8.4

linked_prs.title: [Platform][Gemini] Fix choice conversion logic for `executableCode` and `codeExecutionResult`
linked_prs.body:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Bug fix?      | yes
| New feature?  | no
| Docs?         | no
| Issues        | Fix #422
| License       | MIT

This PR fixes a crash in the **Gemini** ResultConverter when handling responses that only contained executableCode and codeExecutionResult parts.

Before: 
- RuntimeException: Unsupported finish reason "STOP"

After:
- Proper conversion into a TextResult containing formatted code blocks and the last successful OUTCOME_OK output.
- No more exceptions for valid Gemini responses.

What’s Changed
- Enhanced choice conversion logic in ResultConverter::convertChoice():
- Single part → keep legacy behavior (functionCall, text, or one code/output part).
- Multiple parts → aggregate:
- executableCode → Markdown code blocks.
- codeExecutionResult (OUTCOME_OK) → output block.
- Parts flagged as thought: true are ignored for text/code, but their successful execution results are preserved.

New unit tests:
- Covers the failing payload where all parts were marked thought: true.
- Ensures the result is a readable TextResult instead of an exception.

Why
- Prevents crashes when Gemini outputs reasoning steps as thought: true.
- Keeps only useful information (code + last valid output).
- Maintains backward compatibility for simpler responses.

Impact
- No BC breaks — existing behavior for single-part responses unchanged.
- Improved UX — users now see clean Markdown code + output instead of runtime errors.

ai_judgment.response:
Yes.  
This is an agent issue because it involves an error in handling the LLM provider's (Gemini) model output ("finish reason"), specifically within the agent's result conversion logic. It matches the "Incorrect model output handlers" sub-category under LLM operation issues.

linked_prs.title: Fix OpenAI empty choices panic
linked_prs.body:
### Summary

Fixed a panic error ("index out of bounds") that occurred when Goose interacted with OpenAI-compatible servers (like `mlx_lm.server` or `LM Studio`). The error was triggered when these servers sent response chunks with an empty `choices` array, as the code accessed elements like `response["choices"][0]` and `chunk.choices[0]` without checking if the array was empty first. The issue occurs rarely and is now almost guranteed to not occur.

---
### Root Cause Analysis (RCA, perhaps)

The panic was caused by unsafe array access in the OpenAI response parsing logic:

* **Streaming responses**: The `response_to_streaming_message()` function directly accessed `chunk.choices[0]` without performing a bounds check.
* **Non-streaming responses**: The `response_to_message()` function directly accessed `response["choices"][0]["message"]` without validating the array's existence or length.

While an empty `choices` array is valid according to the OpenAI specification, the existing code did not handle this case, leading to a crash.

---
### Technical Solution

Defensive bounds checking was implemented in both response parsing pathways to prevent the crash:

* **Streaming Response Handler (`response_to_streaming_message`)**
    * Added `!chunk.choices.is_empty()` guards before all accesses to `choices[0]`.
    * Added `!tool_chunk.choices.is_empty()` checks within tool call processing loops.
    * Replaced direct access with safe pattern matching and bounds validation.

* **Non-Streaming Response Handler (`response_to_message`)**
    * Added explicit validation using `response.get("choices").and_then(|c| c.as_array())`.
    * Included checks for empty arrays with descriptive error messages.
    * Switched from direct indexing to safe array access methods.

---
### Type of Change

- [ ] Feature
- [x] **Bug fix**
- [ ] Refactor / Code quality
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Build / Release
- [ ] Other

---
### Testing

The fix was verified through the following steps:

* The project was built successfully using `cargo build`.
* Tests were conducted with an LM Studio server using both streaming and non-streaming requests.
* Confirmed that responses with empty `choices` arrays no longer cause panics.
* Verified that standard OpenAI API responses continue to work correctly.

Manual testing confirmed that Goose now gracefully handles empty `choices` arrays, ensuring compatibility with a wider range of OpenAI-compatible servers.

I can't actually test mlx server based but reverified with everything else. (needs apple chip)

---
### Related Issues

Fixes #4276 

---

This issue involves an agent system (goose) failing to interact with an OpenAI-compatible LLM provider (mlx_lm.server) due to a panic in provider-specific code. It references model integration, provider parameters, and LLM operation—all agent issue criteria.

title: self.inference_engine_client.sleep() deallocates memory and causes invalid memory access
body: Our training setup (see all params in the attached [run_tbench_megatron.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22757586/run_tbench_megatron.sh)): - H200x8 / B200x8 (crashes on both) - Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct - train_batch_size=8, n_samples_per_prompt=8, trainer.max_prompt_length=16000, generator.sampling_params.max_generate_length=16000 - Collocated mode - Training Terminal Bench tasks with the new sandbox format. See changes in this PR: https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/414. We are consistently running into invalid memory issues in vLLM during training with the following stack trace: ``` [36m(AsyncVLLMInferenceEngine pid=127749)[0m [08:52:36.868726] coredump: Detected an exception of type CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS (14) [36m(AsyncVLLMInferenceEngine pid=127749)[0m [08:52:36.868733] coredump: - Device: 0 [36m(AsyncVLLMInferenceEngine pid=127749)[0m [08:52:36.868735] coredump: - SM: 142 [36m(AsyncVLLMInferenceEngine pid=127749)[0m [08:52:36.868737] coredump: - Warp: 0 [36m(AsyncVLLMInferenceEngine pid=127749)[0m [08:52:36.868738] coredump: - PC 0x7af21f5dc740 [36m(AsyncVLLMInferenceEngine pid=127749)[0m [08:52:36.877622] coredump: Stack trace (lane masks: active 0xFFFFFFFF, valid 0xFFFFFFFF): [36m(AsyncVLLMInferenceEngine pid=127749)[0m [08:52:36.877666] coredump: #0 0x7af21f5dc7a0 triton_red_fused__to_copy_add_embedding_mean_mul_pow_rsqrt_0 ``` We found an [issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/24879) on the vLLM GitHub repo with similar stack trace (job died during `triton_red_fused__to_copy_add_embedding_mean_mul_pow_rsqrt_0`). The root cause was that `sleep()`, which deallocates the weights of the model from GPU memory, called while there are in-flight requests that still need these weights. We also noticed that the crash always occurs right after `generate()` is done, `sleep()` is called on the inference engine, and training begins. Inspecting the trace further, we found that the vLLM scheduler still has two running requests when the engine died, which matched the reported root cause from the bug above. ``` [36m(AsyncVLLMInferenceEngine pid=1963103)[0m [1;36m(EngineCore_0 pid=1964303)[0;0m ERROR 10-08 04:55:27 [dump_input.py:79] Dumping scheduler stats: SchedulerStats(num_running_reqs=2, num_waiting_reqs=0, step_counter=0, current_wave=0, kv_cache_usage=0.20025836915606832, prefix_cache_stats=PrefixCacheStats(reset=False, requests=0, queries=0, hits=0), spec_decoding_stats=None, num_corrupted_reqs=0) ``` To confirm, we added a hack directly to the `sleep()` [method](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/31a4b3e6c40278025664169eafbc8165e1d0c393/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L416) of vLLM to wait for 60 seconds before aborting all running requests: And we were able to train smoothly without the invalid memory access issue. Some more observations: - From our logging we still see requests being sent to vLLM even after generation finishes and these are the in-flight requests that cause invalid memory access. We still don't know where these in-flight requests are coming from. `self.inference_engine_client.sleep()` is called after generation is done, so at that point the Generator shouldn't be sending more requests to vLLM. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/24879 indicates that the invalid memory access occurs when data_parallel but it's set to 1 for vLLM. - This seems to be triggered by high load, e.g. we didn't see this issue occurring on our setup with train_batch_size=1, n_samples_per_prompt=4.

title: [AI Bundle][Store] Document Indexing Pipeline

A common scenario is to
* **load** documents from a specific source (e.g. folder of PDFs, set of entities, URLs, ...)
* **transform** them (e.g. split into chunks, normalize language, summarize, ...)

* **store** them in a vector store

A configuration for this could for example look like this:

```yaml
ai:

              source: 'string' or ['array', 'of', 'string']
```
