linked_prs.title: Fixes Gemini API parse issue by converting nullable type arrays to single types in tool schemas
linked_prs.body: ## Summary Fixes issue where Gemini API rejected tool schemas containing type arrays like ["string", "null"]. Gemini's API expects type fields to be single string values. The root cause was in the process_map function, which was cloning values for most keys instead of calling process_value. The process_value function already had logic to convert type arrays to single values, but it was only being called for specific keys (properties, items, anyOf, allOf), not for the type key itself. ### Type of Change - [ ] Feature - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Refactor / Code quality - [ ] Performance improvement - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Tests - [ ] Security fix - [ ] Build / Release - [ ] Other (specify below) ### Testing I manually reproduced the issue using Gemini 2.5 Flash as the provider, then tested again with this change to verify the fix. The documentation example at [Graphiti Azure OpenAI integration](https://help.getzep.com/graphiti/graphiti/installation#using-graphiti-with-azure-openai) does not include the necessary `LLMConfig` when initializing `OpenAIClient` with custom model names.

I had to go into internals of graphiti to understand how it works and there were issues [here](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/main/graphiti_core/llm_client/openai_client.py#L108-L111)

To fix this, the example should show explicit use of `LLMConfig(model=..., small_model=...)` with the appropriate Azure deployment names.

Here is a MRE

```py
import asyncio
import os
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from graphiti_core import Graphiti
from graphiti_core.cross_encoder.openai_reranker_client import OpenAIRerankerClient
from graphiti_core.embedder.openai import OpenAIEmbedder, OpenAIEmbedderConfig
from graphiti_core.llm_client.client import LLMConfig
from graphiti_core.llm_client.openai_client import OpenAIClient
from graphiti_core.nodes import EpisodeType
from openai import AsyncAzureOpenAI


async def test_azure_deployments():
    azure_openai_client = AsyncAzureOpenAI(
        api_key=os.getenv("AZURE_LLM_API_KEY"),
        api_version=os.getenv("AZURE_LLM_API_VERSION"),
        azure_endpoint=os.getenv("AZURE_LLM_ENDPOINT"),
    )
    azure_llm_config = LLMConfig(
        small_model="gpt-4o-mini",
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
    )

    graphiti = Graphiti(
        "bolt://localhost:7687",
        "neo4j",
        "password",
        llm_client=OpenAIClient(
            config=azure_llm_config,
            client=azure_openai_client,
        ),
        embedder=OpenAIEmbedder(
            config=OpenAIEmbedderConfig(
                embedding_model="text-embedding-3-small",
            ),
            client=azure_openai_client,
        ),
        cross_encoder=OpenAIRerankerClient(
            config=azure_llm_config,
            client=azure_openai_client,
        ),
    )

    try:
        await graphiti.add_episode(
            name="rippletide_short_description",
            episode_body="Rippletide is a company that is building Sales AGI.",
            source=EpisodeType.text,
            source_description="company information",
            reference_time=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Episode error: {e}")
    else:
        print("✅ Episode added")


asyncio.run(test_azure_deployments())
```

linked_prs.title: fix: prevent repeated 404 errors when accessing deleted sessions
linked_prs.body:
## Summary
When a session is deleted (e.g., from the sessions list), the user might still have the session ID in their URL. Instead of showing a fatal error, we:
1. Detect when initialization fails due to a missing session (404/Session not found)
2. Clear the problematic session ID from the URL
3. Retry initialization without a session ID to create a fresh session
4. Only show a fatal error if the retry also fails

This prevents users from getting stuck on "Agent init failure: [object Object]" which is a "Session not found" error when they try to access deleted session.
 
When sessions are deleted, we maintain a Set of deleted session IDs to avoid repeatedly trying to access them. This prevents "Agent init failure: [object Object]" which can also be multiple 404 errors and provides a smoother user experience.

Key behaviors:
- Skip resume attempts for known deleted sessions
- Clear deleted sessions from URL parameters when detected
 - Mark sessions as deleted when resume attempts fail with 404
- Reset tracking when user starts a new chat session

linked_prs.title: fix(langgraph): fix PostgresSaver crashing when loading older checkpoints
linked_prs.body:
### Description

https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/issues/6137 and https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/issues/5677 reported issues where older checkpoints read by AsyncPostgresSaver/PostgresSaver from `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres==2.0.19` fail to read channel values, throwing `NoneType object is not a mapping`. This was due to a bug in how `channel_values` is assembled:
```python
"channel_values": {
    **value["checkpoint"].get("channel_values"),  # <--- if channel_values doesn't exist (old checkpoint), **None errors
    **self._load_blobs(value["channel_values"]),
},
```
This bug was observed for checkpoints generated by `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres<=2.0.19`.

Fixed by providing a fallback to `value["checkpoint"].get("channel_values")`:
```python
**value["checkpoint"],
"channel_values": {
    **(
        value["checkpoint"].get("channel_values") or {}
    ),  # 'or {}' needed for backwards compat with v3 checkpoints and below, as v4 introduced channel_values key
    **self._load_blobs(value["channel_values"]),
},
```

### Tests
Added test for AsyncPostgresSaver and test for PostgresSaver, using monkeypatch to remove `channel_values` before CheckpointTuple is assembled in `_load_checkpoint_tuple`.

### Solves
https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/issues/6137 and https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/issues/5677

ai_judgment.response: Yes. The issue involves memory-related symptoms, specifically incorrect storage and reading of agent graph state checkpoints, which aligns with the "Memory content errors" sub-category in the taxonomy.

title: Anthropic - input tokens + `max_tokens` > context length
body:
When using the Anthropic provider and reaching the upper limits of the available context length, we can end up in scenarios where the input tokens + the max_tokens value is > than the max supported context length for a given model.

To fix this, we need to keep in consideration the length of the input and set  an appropriate `max_tokens` value before sending requests to the Anthropic API

Example error
```json
400 Bad Request

{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "message": "input length and `max_tokens` exceed context limit: 178959 + 64000 > 200000, decrease input length or `max_tokens` and try again"
  },
  "request_id":"req_011CUB2XUHWkFnQzxcKBbjpF"
}
```

```

Closes #569

linked_prs.title: fix(checkpoint): handle metadata.writes when serializing old checkpoints with Jsonb
linked_prs.body:
Issue

Support for `Checkpoint.metadata.writes` was dropped in `langgraph` v0.5.x. 

In `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres` v2.0.23, metadata was serialized with `BasePostgresSaver._dump_metadata` -> `JsonPlusSerializer.dumps` which handles `pydantic.BaseModel`.

In v2.0.23, metadata is serialized with `psycopg.types.json.Jsonb`, which raises `TypeError: Object of type AIMessage is not JSON serializable` when trying to serialize `writes`.

Solution

- Add `BaseCheckpointSaver.get_serializable_checkpoint_metadata` which pops the `writes` key. 
- Log deprecation warning when strange version combinations are used 

Solves https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/issues/5769

ai_judgment.response: Yes. The issue involves memory-related symptoms, specifically the failure to serialize an AIMessage object when using PostgresSaver for memory storage. This aligns with the "Memory content errors" sub-category under memory-related issues in agent systems.

title: Claude Code provider incorrectly calculate used context token count (much higher than actual)
body:
### What happened?

The Claude Code provider was overwriting token counts with each assistant message instead of accumulating them across the response stream. Counterintuitively, this resulted in __significantly inflated token usage reporting__, with Cline showing much higher context usage than actual consumption.

__Expected:__ Token counts should accurately reflect actual usage as reported by the Claude Code CLI.


### Steps to reproduce

- Use Claude Code provider for a conversation
- Monitor context window usage displayed in Cline
- Run `ccusage` CLI tool to check actual token consumption
- Observe Cline reports much higher usage than actual CLI consumption

### Relevant API REQUEST output

```shell
Before fix:
- Cline reports: Significantly inflated token count
- ccusage shows: Lower actual token consumption
- Discrepancy: Major over-reporting of usage

After fix (PR #[pending]):
- Cline reports match ccusage output exactly
- Token deltas between requests align perfectly
```

### Provider/Model

claude-code/claude-sonnet-4

### System Information

Operating System: macOS
Hardware: Mac (Apple Silicon)

### Cline Version

3.26.2

linked_prs.title: Fix: Corrected token counting in Claude Code provider to prevent doub…
linked_prs.body: ### Related Issue **Issue:** #5792 ### Description The Claude Code provider was incorrectly overwriting token counts instead of accumulating them across multiple assistant messages within a single response stream. This caused significantly inflated token usage reporting, with Cline displaying much higher context usage than actual consumption. **The fix** restores proper token accumulation logic by reverting to using `+=` operators instead of `=` for all token count fields (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`). ### Test Procedure **Testing approach:** - Used the `ccusage` CLI tool to measure actual token consumption by Claude Code - Compared Cline's reported context usage against actual CLI usage - Tested both before and after the fix across multiple conversation turns **Results:** - **Before fix**: Cline reported significantly inflated token counts compared to actual usage - **After fix**: Token counts match `ccusage` measurements exactly - Token deltas between requests now align perfectly with CLI measurements **Confidence:** The fix has been validated to ensure accurate token reporting that matches the underlying CLI's actual consumption. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [ ] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [ ] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots Not applicable - backend token counting fix with no UI changes. ### Additional Notes A separate investigation revealed up to ~20k token overhead between Claude Code and direct Anthropic API providers. This appears to be related to how the Claude Code CLI handles caching and session management. This overhead remains unaddressed by this fix and may warrant future investigation. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes token counting in `ClaudeCodeHandler` by changing assignment to accumulation for token fields, ensuring accurate usage reporting. > > - **Behavior**: > - Fixes token counting in `ClaudeCodeHandler` in `claude-code.ts` by changing `=` to `+=` for `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, and `cacheWriteTokens`. > - Ensures token counts accumulate across multiple assistant messages instead of being overwritten. > - **Testing**: > - Validated using `ccusage` CLI tool to compare reported and actual token usage. > - Confirmed accurate token reporting post-fix. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 5f51dd3961bd4c010f0d0868ea4490a7d92bb7b8. You can [customize](https://app.ellipsis.dev/cline/settings/summaries) this summary. It will automatically update as commits are pushed.

title: [FEATURE] Add Configurable LLM Timeout
body: The timeout is hard coded to 180 [seconds]. When running a low-budget setup, the models can run very slow and timeout. We should have a configurable timeout via ENV variable, while 180 can still be the default setting.

linked_prs.title: Add Configurable LLM Request Timeout via Environment Variable
linked_prs.body:
Previously, LLM request timeouts were hardcoded to 180 seconds (3 minutes) throughout the codebase. This caused issues when:
- Using reasoning models that require longer processing times
- Running on slower local models (Ollama, LMStudio)
- Network latency is higher than expected

The hardcoded timeout was too short for production use cases and couldn't be adjusted without code changes.

### What Changed

Added `LLM_TIMEOUT` environment variable to control request timeouts globally:
- **Default:** 600 seconds (10 minutes) - increased from 180 seconds
- **Configurable:** Set via environment variable for different deployment scenarios
- **Consistent:** Applied uniformly across all LLM API calls

Fixes #94, Closes #86, Closes #58

from langgraph.checkpoint.postgres import PostgresSaver

from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage


PG_URI = os.environ.get(
    "PG_URI",

        print("Raised:", repr(exc))
        # re-raise for full traceback in CI/issue
        raise
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
redacted Object of type HumanMessage is not JSON serializable') redacted
```

### Description

### Summary
Upgrading `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres` from 2.0.21 to 2.0.22 breaks metadata serialization. Code that saved checkpoints with non‑JSON objects in metadata (e.g., `HumanMessage`) now raises “Object of type HumanMessage is not JSON serializable.”

### What I’m doing
Saving a checkpoint with `PostgresSaver.put(...)` where the `metadata` includes a LangChain `HumanMessage`.

### Expected behavior
- Same behavior as 2.0.21: metadata accepted (JsonPlus previously handled complex Python objects), or clear migration guidance if behavior is intentionally changed.

### Actual behavior
- On 2.0.22, calling `put(...)` raises:
  - Exception: “Object of type HumanMessage is not JSON serializable”

### Minimal reproducible example
```python
import os
from langgraph.checkpoint.postgres import PostgresSaver
from langgraph.checkpoint.base import empty_checkpoint
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage

PG_URI = os.getenv(
    "PG_URI",
    "postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable",
)

config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "thread-mre", "checkpoint_ns": ""}}
checkpoint = empty_checkpoint()
metadata = {
    "source": "input",
    "step": 1,
    "writes": {},
    "message": HumanMessage(content="hello world"),  # non-JSON object
}

with PostgresSaver.from_conn_string(PG_URI) as saver:
    saver.setup()
    saver.put(config, checkpoint, metadata, {})  # 2.0.22 -> raises; 2.0.21 -> OK
```

### Environment
- Works: `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres==2.0.21`
- Fails: `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres==2.0.22`
- Python 3.10+/3.11
- psycopg 3 (binary/pool)
- OS: Linux
- Postgres: local instance

### Additional notes
- In 2.0.21, metadata was serialized via JsonPlus (tolerated Python objects).
- In 2.0.22, metadata is passed directly as JSONB (`Jsonb(get_checkpoint_metadata(...))`), which rejects non‑JSON objects.
- If this change is intended, please document it and provide a migration note (e.g., require JSON-only metadata or recommend moving complex objects to channel blobs).

title: KeyError when invoking a RunnableCallable with a config param
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question. For questions, please use the LangChain Forum (https://forum.langchain.com/).
- [x] I added a clear and detailed title that summarizes the issue.
- [x] I read what a minimal reproducible example is (https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example).
- [x] I included a self-contained, minimal example that demonstrates the issue INCLUDING all the relevant imports. The code run AS IS to reproduce the issue.

### Example Code

```python
import os
from typing import TypedDict

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig

class State(TypedDict):
    messages: list[str]


def fetch_foo(*, config: RunnableConfig) -> str:
    """A simple tool which gets 'foo'
    """
    return config["configurable"]["foo"]

def build_graph():
    chat_model = ChatOpenAI(
        model_name="gpt-4o"
    )
    chat_model = chat_model.bind_tools([fetch_foo])
    tool_node = ToolNode([fetch_foo])
    graph = StateGraph(State)

    def node_a(state):
        message = chat_model.invoke(state["messages"][-1], config={"callbacks": [CallbackHandler()]})
        state = {"messages": state["messages"] + [message]}
        tool_node.invoke(input=state, config={"callbacks": [CallbackHandler()]})  # note the config param here
        return state

    graph.add_node("agent", node_a)
    graph.add_node("tools", tool_node)
    graph.set_entry_point("agent")
    graph.add_conditional_edges(
        "agent",
        lambda x: "tools" if x["messages"][-1].tool_calls else "__end__",
    )
    graph.add_edge("tools", "__end__")
    graph.set_finish_point("agent")
    return graph.compile()

def main():
    graph = build_graph()
    print(graph.invoke({"messages": ["Call fetch_foo and give me the result"]}, config={"configurable": {"foo": "bar"}}))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/cwd/test.py", line 61, in <module>
    main()
  File "/cwd/test.py", line 58, in main
    print(graph.invoke({"messages": ["Call fetch_foo and give me the result"]}, config={"configurable": {"foo": "bar"}}))
  File "/cwd/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/__init__.py", line 2844, in invoke
    for chunk in self.stream(
  File "/cwd/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/__init__.py", line 2534, in stream
    for _ in runner.tick(
  File "/cwd/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/runner.py", line 162, in tick
    run_with_retry(
  File "/cwd/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/retry.py", line 42, in run_with_retry
    return task.proc.invoke(task.input, config)
  File "/cwd/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/langgraph/utils/runnable.py", line 623, in invoke
    input = context.run(step.invoke, input, config, **kwargs)
  File "/cwd/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/langgraph/utils/runnable.py", line 377, in invoke
    ret = self.func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/cwd/test.py", line 42, in node_a
    tool_node.invoke(input=state, config={"callbacks": [CallbackHandler()]})  # note the config param here
  File "/cwd/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/langgraph/utils/runnable.py", line 333, in invoke
    _conf = config[CONF]
KeyError: 'configurable'
```

### Description

When using a `RunnableCallable`, eg, `ToolNode`, and invoking it with a config that doesn't have a `configurable` key, eg, passing in `langfuse.langchain.CallbackHandler` to the `callbacks` config, we hit a KeyError. A workaround is adding a `configurable` key with `{}` as the value to the config you're passing in

I believe the solution would be doing
```
config = ensure_config(config)
```
instead of
```
if config is None:
        config = ensure_config()
```
in `invoke`/`ainvoke` as `ensure_config` will handle a `None` config fine and if the `config` arg isn't `None`, we merge it before doing `_conf = config[CONF]`

title: Enhancement: Add log truncation options to `get_job_logs` tool for improved LLM context efficiency
body:
## Summary

The `get_job_logs` tool currently returns complete job logs, which can be extremely long and inefficient when used as MCP tool context for LLMs. Adding log truncation options like `tail_lines`  parameters would help focus on relevant failure information.

## Problem

When debugging CI/CD failures using the `get_job_logs` tool in LLM conversations:

1. **Context Overflow**: Complete job logs can easily exceed LLM context limits
2. **Information Overload**: Most debugging scenarios only need the final portion where failures occur
4. **Poor User Experience**: Long logs make it harder to identify specific failure points

## Proposed Solution

Add optional truncation parameters to the `get_job_logs` tool:

- `tail_lines`: Return last N lines (most useful for failure debugging)

Example usage:
```json
{
  "name": "get_job_logs",
  "arguments": {
    "owner": "example",
    "repo": "repo", 
    "job_id": 12345,
    "tail_lines": 100,
    "return_content": true
  }
}
```



This enhancement aligns with existing concerns about LLM context efficiency, similar to Issue #142 regarding excessive context size.

linked_prs.body: ### Related Issue - https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/6204 - https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/6203 - https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/6202 - https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/6172 - https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/6159 - https://www.reddit.com/r/CLine/comments/1nfkxep/cline_3282_stuck_at_loading/ ### Description Slack dump: The user reported that API Request is stuck at 'Loading...'. The order of events for a first request in task/index is `recursivelyMakeClineRequests` -> `api_req_started` "Loading..." -> `ensureCheckpointInitialized` -> `this.checkpointManager.commit()` -> `loadContext` I'm assuming that checkpoints are not the issue here since they timeout after 15s and the user reported the request hangs infinitely while on old versions it doesnt. I investigated the loadContext function and compared the diff of v3.26.6 and 3.28 - some change that was made here that was the cause of the issue. The github issue showed the error "toLowerCase is not a function" so something in loadContext eventually calls this function on an object that isn't a string. the trace is loadContext -> Promise.all -> Promise.all The only flow where a second promise.all is called is when processUserContent is called in loadContext, which calls parseMentions and parseSlashCommands. I believe one of these two functions is causing the failure/hang ie we now pass in this.focusChainSettings to the parseSlashCommands function Eventually I traced the error to this: ``` isPowerShell = detectedShell != null && typeof detectedShell === "string" && (detectedShell.toLowerCase().includes("powershell") || detectedShell.toLowerCase().includes("pwsh")) ``` - the bug only happened to people on windows - and it happened in loadcontext -> parseslashcommands - and the new changes here were the deepplanning stuff ### Test Procedure I pulled up a diff from v3.27 and v3.28 and found that we made some changes to parseSlashCommands in loadContext. linked_prs.body: ### Related Issue **Issue:** #6192 ### Description Currently, orchestration is failing for requests to GPT-5 that include the `max_tokens` parameter (a future fix for orchestration will support GPT-5 with this deprecated parameter). This happens because the GPT-5 model family rejects the deprecated `max_tokens` parameter - only `max_completion_tokens` is accepted for reasoning models (such as GPT-5). More details can be found here: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/5072518-controlling-the-length-of-openai-model-responses#h_930bf1dfa4 The original reason for adding the `max_tokens` parameter was to support the Anthropic model family. That issue was resolved a week ago, so this parameter is no longer required. If, in the future, we allow users to configure model parameters directly in the SAP AI Core provider, we will need to return the `model_params` field. ### Test Procedure - I tested that all models are working in orchestration mode ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots ### Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Remove `model_params` from `LlmModuleConfig` in `SapAiCoreHandler` to support GPT-5 models in orchestration mode. > > - **Behavior**: > - Remove `model_params` from `LlmModuleConfig` in `SapAiCoreHandler` to support GPT-5 models in orchestration mode. > - Addresses issue where GPT-5 models reject deprecated `max_tokens` parameter. > - **Misc**: > - Update changeset to reflect removal of `model_params` in orchestration mode. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for aca82ce088a26b2218fdd8c05b7ea68d1f167cbe. title: task.result not populated when creating thread with supersteps
body:
### Privileged issue

- [x] I am a LangGraph maintainer, or was asked directly by a LangGraph maintainer to create an issue here.

### Description

When creating a thread from supersteps:
```python
thread = await client.threads.create(graph_id="graph", supersteps=supersteps)
```
the API response does not populate `task.result`, which captures the state update that occurred as a result of that task's execution.

This causes bugs when cloning and forking in LG Studio. Previously `metadata.writes` was included in the response from creating a thread and we got the necessary information to properly render the thread history from there. Now this never gets returned, as `metadata.writes` was deprecated in LG 0.5.x. In Studio we have logic to look either in `metadata.writes` or `task.results`  for the necessary info, so to fix this we need to properly populate `task.result`.

linked_prs.title: fix(langgraph): fix supersteps not populating task.result field
linked_prs.body:
### Description

Fix `bulk_update_state` and `abulk_update_state` so history populates `tasks[*].result` when creating state via supersteps.

There was a branch in these functions that I'm guessing was meant to be triggered when a `StateUpdate.as_node` was the name of a real node (not `"__input__"` or `"__copy__"`), but was never being triggered because of a condition `CONFIG_KEY_CHECKPOINT_ID not in config[CONF]`:
```python
# apply pending writes, if not on specific checkpoint
if (
    CONFIG_KEY_CHECKPOINT_ID not in config[CONF]
    and saved is not None
    and saved.pending_writes
):
    next_tasks = prepare_next_tasks(...)
```

From what I can tell, in the bulk-update flow every superstep carries a `checkpoint_id`, so the condition was always false. That skipped `prepare_next_tasks(...)` and prevented us from discovering the task IDs that we would need to attach the task result. So, I removed this check.

I also replaced the `pending_writes` check with a more lenient one (just check it is not None to satisfy type checkers). I found that `saved.pending_writes` was sometimes just `[]`, and in this case we would skip `prepare_next_tasks(...)` and never attach the task result. 

Now for each task discovered in `prepare_next_tasks(...)`, I collect the task IDs and reuse them when running all writers of the chosen node (applying the updates). 

### Tests

- `test_supersteps_populate_task_results` for `PregelLoop` and `AsyncPregelLoop`
 
These tests build a single node graph and compare history from two threads: one uses `.invoke` and the other is build from supersteps. Both tests fail on main and pass with this PR.

### Issue

title: Kimi will truncate a long file when edit  cause max_token exceed.
body: ### Plugin Type VSCode Extension ### Cline Version v3.28.6 ### What happened? When using the Kimi model provided by moonshot.cn to edit documents, if the output document length is too long, Kimi will truncate the document output and repeatedly retry the editing request. Based on local debugging results, this occurs because the maximum output length for the response has been reached. According to the documentation provided by Moonshot: https://platform.moonshot.cn/docs/guide/faq#kimi-api-%E8%BF%94%E5%9B%9E%E7%9A%84%E5%86%85%E5%AE%B9%E4%B8%8D%E5%AE%8C%E6%95%B4%E6%88%96%E8%A2%AB%E6%88%AA%E6%96%AD and https://platform.moonshot.cn/docs/api/chat#%E8%AF%B7%E6%B1%82%E5%86%85%E5%AE%B9 It can be concluded that when the request does not specify `max_tokens`, Kimi will use a default `max_tokens` value. If the model's required output length exceeds `max_tokens`, the model will truncate the output. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Select any model provided by moonshot.cn. 2. Requesting the model to generate or edit a large file (typically over 3000 characters), such as converting a large CSV file to a JSON file. 3. watching the model generate the file. It will truncate the file and retry. ### Provider/Model moonshot:kimi-k2-0905-preview ### System Information OS: macOS 26 CPU: Apple M1

linked_prs.title: PR: Support Auto-Complete Based on Past History (#638)
linked_prs.body:
### **Title**

Add Inline Suggestion Support to TUI Chat Editor
solves #638
---

### **Summary**

This PR introduces inline suggestion (auto-complete) support in the TUI chat editor, allowing users to press **Tab** to accept contextually relevant completions drawn from their recent message history.

---

### **Changes**

#### **1. History Enhancements**

* **File:** `pkg/history/history.go`
* Added a new function:

  ```go
  LatestMatch(prefix string)
  ```

  * Scans message history from newest to oldest.
  * Returns the latest entry that extends the current prefix, or the last message if no prefix is provided.
  * Imports `strings` for prefix matching.

#### **2. Editor Suggestion Logic**

* **File:** `pkg/tui/components/editor/editor.go`
* Added imports: `regexp`, `lipgloss`, `runewidth`.
* Introduced new state fields:

  * `suggestion`
  * `hasSuggestion`
  * `cursorHidden`
* Implemented helper functions to:

  * Strip ANSI prompts.
  * Detect the active input line.
  * Render a ghost overlay using layered lipgloss canvases.
  * Refresh or clear suggestion state.
* Editor behavior updates:

  * Suggestions refresh after **send**, **up/down**, and each **update cycle**.
  * Cursor hides when a suggestion ghost is visible.
  * Added `AcceptSuggestion()` to commit a suggestion when invoked.

#### **3. Chat Page Integration**

* **File:** `pkg/tui/page/chat/chat.go`
* When the editor panel is focused and **Tab** is pressed:

  * If a suggestion exists, `AcceptSuggestion()` is called.
  * The completion is inserted inline without losing focus.

#### **4. Styling**

* **File:** `pkg/tui/styles/styles.go`
* Added `SuggestionGhostStyle` (muted foreground) for overlay rendering.
* Preserves existing `EditorStyle` padding.

---

### **Result**

Users now experience contextual inline suggestions in the chat editor.
As they type, the latest matching history entry appears as a muted inline “ghost.”
Pressing **Tab** confirms and inserts the suggestion seamlessly.

title: Discussions toolset: add author.login, updated_at in response; and orderBy in parameters
body:
I prepared this Issue with Claude Code and edited/reviewed it heavily, but did not audit its specific code references, so apologies if e.g. line numbers are not quite precise; consider it pseudocode but hopefully it's pretty actionable.

Related to: https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/issues/671 (but I broke this out because 670 here should be less controversial/very aligned with current designs)

### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

I'm building out some workflows that will pull and summarize Discussions, and some notably missing pieces that I think make sense to add from a tool design perspective to `list_discussions` are readily available in the GraphQL API:

Current missing data in `list_discussions` (pkg/github/discussions.go:71-78, 110-118):
- `author.login` information in response
- `updatedAt` field in response (only `createdAt`)
- `orderBy` parameter (can't sort by UPDATED_AT)
- `direction` parameter (can't control ASC/DESC)

This makes it difficult to:
1. Find recently active discussions (those with new comments/updates)
2. Know who started discussions without making out of band API calls

### Proposed solution

**1. Add missing fields to the GraphQL query** (pkg/github/discussions.go:71-78):
```go
Nodes []struct {
    Number    githubv4.Int
    Title     githubv4.String
    CreatedAt githubv4.DateTime
    UpdatedAt githubv4.DateTime  // Add
    Author    struct {           // Add
        Login githubv4.String
    }
    Category  struct {
        Name githubv4.String
    }
    URL githubv4.String `graphql:"url"`
}
```

**2. Add orderBy parameters to the tool definition** (pkg/github/discussions.go:16-34):
```go
mcp.WithString("orderBy",
    mcp.Description("Sort discussions by field"),
    mcp.Enum("CREATED_AT", "UPDATED_AT"),
),
mcp.WithString("direction", 
    mcp.Description("Sort direction"),
    mcp.Enum("ASC", "DESC"),
),
```

**3. Update the GraphQL query to use ordering** (pkg/github/discussions.go:80, 119):
```go
} `graphql:"discussions(first: 100, orderBy: $orderBy)"`
```

The GitHub GraphQL API fully supports these fields, as demonstrated:
```graphql
query {
  repository(owner: "vercel", name: "next.js") {
    discussions(first: 3, orderBy: {field: UPDATED_AT, direction: DESC}) {
      nodes {
        number
        title
        createdAt
        updatedAt
        author {
          login
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

1. **"Show me discussions that have been updated in the last 24 hours"**
   - Sort by UPDATED_AT, then filter client-side by date

2. **"List the most recently active discussions with their authors"**
   - `orderBy: "UPDATED_AT", direction: "DESC"` to get recently active threads
   - Use `author.login` to see who started each discussion

3. **"Monitor discussions started by external contributors"**
   - Filter by author.login to identify non-team discussions
   - Sort by UPDATED_AT to catch new activity

4. **"Generate a weekly discussion activity report"**
   - Sort by UPDATED_AT to find all discussions with recent activity
   - Group by author.login to show top contributors

5. **"Find stale discussions that need attention"**
   - Sort by UPDATED_AT in ASC order
   - Compare updatedAt vs createdAt to find abandoned threads

### Additional context

**Comparison with other tools in the codebase:**
- `list_issues` already has both `sort` (including "updated") and `since` parameters (pkg/github/issues.go:351-361)
- `list_pull_requests` has `sort` with "updated" option (pkg/github/pullrequests.go:356-358)
- Discussions should have feature parity with these other tools

**GraphQL API verification:**
The DiscussionOrderField enum supports both CREATED_AT and UPDATED_AT:
```json
{"name":"CREATED_AT","description":"Order discussions by creation time."},
{"name":"UPDATED_AT","description":"Order discussions by most recent modification time."}

title: Discussions toolset: allow for org-level Discussions to be queried with list_discussions
body:
I prepared this Issue with Claude Code and edited/reviewed it heavily, but did not audit its specific code references, so apologies if e.g. line numbers are not quite precise; consider it pseudocode but hopefully it's pretty actionable.

Related to: https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/issues/670 (but I broke this out since it's perhaps a slightly more controversial design decision to make)

### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Some GitHub organizations host their discussions at the organization level (e.g., https://github.com/orgs/modelcontextprotocol/discussions), but the current GitHub MCP Server's discussions toolset cannot access these discussions. 

**Current limitation:**
- `list_discussions` requires both `owner` and `repo` parameters
- No way to query organization-level discussions
- Users must know the hidden implementation detail that org discussions live in the `.github` repository (and even then, it's not accessible via the MCP server)

Organization discussions appear to be stored in a special `.github` repository within the organization. This can be queried via GraphQL:

```graphql
query {
  repository(owner: "modelcontextprotocol", name: ".github") {
    discussions(first: 3, orderBy: {field: UPDATED_AT, direction: DESC}) {
      nodes {
        number
        title
        url
      }
    }
  }
}
```

This successfully returns discussions like:
- 493: "Reconnection should re-send initialization"
- 492: "Order of Elicitation Parameters"
- 491: "Exclude tools?"

### Proposed solution

**Option 1: Make `repo` parameter optional in `list_discussions`**
When `repo` is omitted, automatically query the `.github` repository:
```go
// In list_discussions handler
if repo == "" {
    repo = ".github"  // Default to org discussions repo
}
```

**Option 2: Create a dedicated `list_organization_discussions` tool**
A new tool specifically for organization-level discussions:
```go
mcp.NewTool("list_organization_discussions",
    mcp.WithDescription("List discussions at the organization level"),
    mcp.WithString("org",
        mcp.Required(),
        mcp.Description("Organization name"),
    ),
    // ... other parameters like orderBy, direction, etc.
)
```

### Example prompts or workflows (for tools/toolsets only)

1. **"Show me all discussions in the modelcontextprotocol organization"**
   - Query org-level discussions without needing to know about `.github` repo

2. **"Monitor community discussions across our entire organization"**
   - Access centralized org discussions for community management

3. **"Find unanswered questions in our organization's Q&A discussions"**
   - Filter org-level discussions by category and state

4. **"Generate a report of most active organization-wide discussions"**
   - Sort org discussions by activity to identify hot topics

5. **"Track discussions from external contributors across the organization"**
   - Monitor org-level discussions for community engagement metrics

The table schema uses dimension-specific embedding columns:

- `embedding_3072`

### Bug Report

Hi,

I'm currently testing the PD performance in SGLang at larger batches. The motivation being, this is a worker profile I expect to encounter in (agentic) chat. I think there is some error, but I struggle to identify the source based on the available logs. 

Steps to replicate on a single H100 node (should also work with less compute if you change the TP size/smaller model):

`run_decode.sh`
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-32B-FP8 --disaggregation-mode decode --port 30001 --host 10.1.0.21 --tp-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2
```

`run_prefill.sh`
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-32B-FP8 --disaggregation-mode prefill --port 30000 --host 10.1.0.21 --tp-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2
```

```bash
python3 -m sglang.srt.disaggregation.mini_lb --prefill http://10.1.0.21:30000 --decode http://10.1.0.21:30001 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8002
```

For a single simple setup this works fine, the problem starts when I try to simulate a batch of long context, e.g. 8x30k tokens in. Than it completely fails

        results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
        print(f"All {len(results)} requests completed")

if __name__ == "__main__":

linked_prs.body: ### Related Issue **Issue:** https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/7183 https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/7224 ### Description Fixes a type error when using OpenAI-compatible servers (like llama.cpp's llama-server) where the `temperature` parameter was being sent as a string instead of a number, causing API errors. ### Problem When using OpenAI-compatible servers such as llama.cpp's llama-server, users encountered errors in the server logs: Wrong type supplied for parameter 'temperature'. Expected 'number', using default value: [json.exception.type_error.302] type must be number, but is string This occurred because the `temperature` value from the model configuration was being passed directly without type coercion. When user settings or configurations store numeric values as strings (which commonly happens with JSON configurations), the API would reject the request or fall back to defaults. ### Solution Modified src/core/api/providers/openai.ts to explicitly convert the `temperature` parameter to a number before passing it to the OpenAI client: **Before:** ```typescript let temperature: number | undefined = this.options.openAiModelInfo?.temperature ?? openAiModelInfoSaneDefaults.temperature ``` ### Test Procedure ensure openai provider works correctly. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots Verified the provider still works with other provider like deepseek ### Additional Notes Changed temperature assignment to explicitly check for undefined and convert the value to Number type before use. linked_prs.title: 🪝Hooks: Exclude .clinerules/hooks/ files from Rules feature
linked_prs.body: ### Related Issue **Issue:** [#7184](https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/7184), [#7185](https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/7185) ### Description I've included three related bug fixes in this PR, two of which were found by Fibi (thank you Fibi!). #### First: Fix for [#7184](https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/7184) Cline's Rules feature was picking up all of the hooks directories as though they're rules config files. The intended behavior is that the hooks directory sits within the `.clinerules/` directory of a given workspace root (and equivalent global Cline Rules directory, and Hooks also supports multi-root), and that the hooks directory is a sibling of the workflows directory and should follow the same special case pattern to be excluded from being detected by Cline Rules. The solution here requires two phases, and this PR is the first phase: * __Phase 1 (immediate fix):__ Prevent hooks files from being picked up by Cline Rules. * __Phase 2 (future PR):__ Implement a UI tab next to the Rules tab and the Workflows tab that detects only hook scripts (properly named, doesn't pick up README.md nor any example hook files) and enable users to toggle each hook on/off using a UI similar to the one in the Rules tab. #### Second: Fix for [#7185](https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/7185) When a directory path contains whitespace the behavior prior to this PR is that the hooks logic cuts off the path at the first whitespace character. This PR fixes that by escaping paths properly during hook directory discovery. For example, if a project directory contains a whitespace as in `My Example Project/` the hooks discovery code treated it as `My/` and the other parts were args. So, now the `My Example Project/` will be interpreted correctly as `My Example Project/`, fully escaped as needed differently for different operating systems, and this will work regardless of which directory type (global versus single root versus multi-root). #### Third The first bug quietly exposed an important detail, and it's good that we're fixing this before the initial release. The global hooks directory was nested under the global cline rules directory, whereas the global workflows directory is a sibling of the cline rules directory. The global hooks directory should follow the same pattern as workflows as a sibling to workflows. This PR fixes this implementation detail. So, instead of `~/Documents/Cline/Rules/Hooks/` we'll now be looking for `~/Documents/Cline/Hooks/`. ### Test Procedure To test I loaded the Cline extension and clicked the scale/justice icon at the bottom of the webview to show the Rules config UI. linked_prs.title: fix: Replace Event ID generation with UUID4 to prevent collisions
linked_prs.body:
Fixes issue #719 where SQLite integrity constraint failures occurred during streaming responses due to duplicate Event IDs.

##  Description
This PR resolves SQLite integrity constraint failures that occur during streaming intermediate responses in FastAPI-only run mode. The error `UNIQUE constraint failed: events.id, events.app_name, events.user_id, events.session_id` was caused by Event ID collisions when agents inform users before calling tools during streaming scenarios.

### Root Cause
The original `Event.new_id()` method generated only 8-character random strings using `random.choice()`, which created a high probability of collisions during rapid event creation in streaming scenarios.

### Solution
- **Replaced** random 8-character string generation with UUID4 in `Event.new_id()`
- **Removed** unused `random` and `string` imports  
- **Added** `uuid` import

##  Changes Made

### Core Changes
- **File**: `src/google/adk/events/event.py`
  - Replaced `Event.new_id()` implementation from random 8-char strings to UUID4
  - Added `import uuid`
  - Removed unused `import random` and `import string`

### Manual E2E Verification
 **Event ID Generation Test**:
```bash
$ cd /workspaces/adk-python && python -c "from src.google.adk.events.event import Event; print('Event ID generation test:'); print(f'ID 1: {Event.new_id()}'); print(f'ID 2: {Event.new_id()}'); print('IDs are different:', Event.new_id() != Event.new_id())"
Event ID generation test:
ID 1: 1a8f6562-822b-4c85-8206-36c895946b44
ID 2: c691ce68-0333-4a8b-af83-c2de39625798
IDs are different: True
```

 **UUID4 Format Verification**: Generated IDs follow proper UUID4 format with version 4 identifier and variant bits
 **Database Compatibility**: UUID strings work seamlessly with existing SQLAlchemy schema (128 char limit)
 **Streaming Scenario**: Simulated rapid event creation no longer produces duplicate IDs

## Performance & Impact

### Before (High Collision Risk)
- **ID Length**: 8 characters
- **Character Set**: 62 chars (a-z, A-Z, 0-9)  
- **Total Combinations**: 62^8 ≈ 218 trillion
- **Collision Probability**: High during rapid event creation (~50% at 500K events)

### After (Virtually No Collision Risk)
- **ID Length**: 36 characters (UUID4 format)
- **Total Combinations**: 2^122 ≈ 5.3 × 10^36
- **Collision Probability**: Negligible (< 1 in 10^18 for billions of events)
- **Performance**: Minimal overhead (UUID generation is very fast)

##  Code Review Notes

### Key Changes Summary
1. **Import Changes**: 
   - Added: `import uuid`
   - Removed: `import random`, `import string`

2. **Method Implementation**:
   ```python
   # Before
   @staticmethod
   def new_id():
       characters = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
       return ''.join(random.choice(characters) for _ in range(8))
   
   # After  
   @staticmethod
   def new_id():
       return str(uuid.uuid4())
   ```

3. **Database Schema Compatibility**: 
   - UUID4 strings (36 chars) fit within existing `String(128)` columns
   - No database migration required
   - Backward compatible with existing Event IDs

### Edge Cases Covered
-  Concurrent event creation across multiple threads
-  Rapid sequential event generation
-  Streaming intermediate responses (original issue scenario)
-  Manual ID assignment preservation
-  ID immutability after creation

##  Acceptance Criteria
- [x] SQLite integrity constraint failures eliminated
- [x] Event IDs are globally unique
- [x] UUID4 format compliance
- [x] Backward compatibility maintained
- [x] No performance degradation
- [x] Comprehensive test coverage
- [x] No regression in existing functionality

##  Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines (pyink/isort)
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Manual E2E testing performed
- [x] No breaking changes
- [x] Related issue linked (#719)

---

**Testing Commands for Reviewers:**

```
# Quick verification
python -c "from src.google.adk.events.event import Event; print([Event.new_id() for _ in range(5)])"
```

title: Bug: SDK Agent Incorrectly Reports Context-Loading Tasks as Failed
body:
## Summary

The claude-mem SDK agent generates incorrect summaries reporting files as "not found" when users request context-loading tasks (e.g., "review and understand files"). Files are successfully read via Read tool, but the SDK agent's system prompt instructs it to skip "file related research" with no deliverable output. These skipped operations are then incorrectly reported as failed file lookups in session summaries.

## Environment

- **claude-mem version**: 5.2.3
- **Claude Code version**: 2.0.36
- **Repository**: thedotmack/claude-mem

## Impact

### Severity: Medium-High

- **Frequency**: Every time users request context-loading tasks ("review", "understand", "learn from")
- **Scope**: Affects research/learning workflows, not action-oriented tasks
- **Memory Pollution**: False "file not found" reports accumulate for legitimate read operations

### Consequences

1. **Incorrect summaries** - Context-loading sessions incorrectly report files as missing when successfully read
2. **Memory database pollution** - Search results contain false "file not found" entries
3. **Workflow confusion** - Users uncertain whether files were actually processed
4. **Missing observations** - Legitimate learning/research activities aren't recorded as observations

### Evidence of Pattern

Users requesting "review and understand" tasks receive summaries like:
- "Files were searched using glob patterns but do not exist in the current repository"
- "No work was completed... prerequisite files could not be found"

Meanwhile, identical file paths in action-oriented tasks ("convert file", "fix file") work correctly, proving files exist and are accessible.

## Steps to Reproduce

### Example 1: Context-Loading Task (FAILS)

1. Create a user prompt requesting understanding/review:

   ```text
   Review and understand the rules from @ai_docs/continuous-improvement/rules.md
   ```

2. Observe that Claude Code successfully reads the file via Read tool
3. Session completes successfully - file content is processed
4. Stop session → Summary incorrectly reports:

   ```text
   Investigated: Attempted to locate and read files. Files were searched using glob
   patterns but do not exist in the current repository.
   Completed: No work was completed... prerequisite files could not be found.
   ```

### Example 2: Action-Oriented Task (WORKS)

1. Create a user prompt requesting an action with deliverable:

   ```text
   Convert .claude/commands/improve.md to an agent
   ```

2. Observe that Claude Code successfully reads the file via Read tool
3. Session completes - agent file is created
4. Stop session → Summary correctly reports:

   ```text
   Investigated: Read and analyzed the improve.md command file
   Completed: Created sub-agent definition at .claude/agents/improve.md
   ```

**Pattern:** Context-loading tasks (no deliverable) are incorrectly reported as failed, while action-oriented tasks (create deliverable) are correctly reported

## Expected Behavior

Context-loading tasks should generate observations and summaries like:

```text
Request: Review and understand continuous improvement rules from @ai_docs/continuous-improvement/rules.md
Investigated: Read and analyzed continuous improvement rules documentation
Learned: Rules emphasize trust-but-verify approach, fix-forward pattern, and systematic debugging
Completed: Established context for development practices including KISS, DRY, YAGNI principles
```

Alternatively, if SDK agent is instructed to skip routine research, the summary should accurately reflect this:

```text
Completed: Reviewed documentation files for context (no deliverable produced)
```

## Actual Behavior

Context-loading tasks are reported as failed file lookups:

```text
Request: Review and understand the rules from @ai_docs/continuous-improvement/rules.md
Investigated: Attempted to locate and read files. Files were searched using glob
patterns but do not exist in the current repository.
Completed: No work was completed... prerequisite files could not be found.
Learned: The source documents... are not yet created or accessible in the system.
```

Files were successfully read via Read tool, but SDK agent reports them as non-existent.

## Root Cause Analysis

### The Problem: Task Classification, Not Path Matching

**Location**: `src/sdk/prompts.ts` - `buildInitPrompt()` function (lines 24-126)

The SDK agent's system prompt contains conflicting guidance about research/learning tasks:

#### 1. Deliverable-Focused Instructions (Lines 27-49)

```typescript
CRITICAL: Record what was BUILT/FIXED/DEPLOYED/CONFIGURED, not what you (the observer) are doing.

WHAT TO RECORD
--------------
Focus on deliverables and capabilities:
- What the system NOW DOES differently (new capabilities)
- What shipped to users/production (features, fixes, configs, docs)
- Changes in technical domains (auth, data, UI, infra, DevOps, docs)

Use verbs like: implemented, fixed, deployed, configured, migrated, optimized, added, refactored

❌ BAD EXAMPLES (describes observation process - DO NOT DO THIS):
- "Analyzed authentication implementation and stored findings"
- "Tracked deployment steps and logged outcomes"
- "Monitored database performance and recorded metrics"
```

#### 2. Skip File Research Instruction (Lines 51-59)

```typescript
WHEN TO SKIP
------------
Skip routine operations:
- Empty status checks
- Package installations with no errors
- Simple file listings
- Repetitive operations you've already documented
- If file related research comes back as empty or not found  ← 🎯 THIS LINE
- **No output necessary if skipping.**
```

### What Actually Happens

**When user requests**: "Review and understand [files]"

1. Claude Code reads files successfully via Read tool ✅
2. User processes file content for context/learning ✅
3. No deliverable artifact is created (by design) ✅
4. SDK agent observes tool executions
5. SDK agent sees this is "file related research" with no deliverable
6. SDK agent: "Skip routine operations... file related research" → Skips creating observation
7. Summary generation: No observation exists → Assumes files weren't found
8. Summary incorrectly reports: "Files do not exist" ❌

### Why Action-Oriented Tasks Work

**When user requests**: "Convert [file] to agent"

1. Claude Code reads file successfully ✅
2. User creates new agent file ✅
3. Deliverable artifact exists ✅
4. SDK agent sees tool executions + file creation
5. SDK agent: "What shipped? New agent file" → Creates observation
6. Summary correctly reports what was built ✅

### The Mismatch

The `discovery` observation type exists (line 74: "learning about existing system"), but the prompt actively discourages using it:
- "DO NOT" record analysis/monitoring activities
- Skip "file related research"
- Focus on deliverables only

Context-loading tasks have nowhere to go in this framework.

### Timeline Evidence

Investigation showed this pattern is consistent:

**File creation:**
- `rules.md`: Created Nov 9, 12:29 AM
- `lessons-learned.md`: Created Nov 8, 8:40 PM

**"Review and understand" requests:**
- Multiple sessions from Nov 9, 2:11 AM onward (files existed for 1+ hours)

**Result:**
- Files successfully read via Read tool ✅
- Summaries reported "files do not exist" ❌
- Pattern consistent across sessions

This proves files existed and were accessible - the issue is task classification, not file availability.

## Suggested Fixes

### Option 1: Clarify "Discovery" Observation Type (Quick Fix)

Update the system prompt in `buildInitPrompt()` to clarify when `discovery` type should be used:

```typescript
// In src/sdk/prompts.ts, around line 68, update the discovery description:

  <type>[ bugfix | feature | refactor | change | discovery | decision ]</type>
  <!--
    **type**: MUST be EXACTLY one of these 6 options (no other values allowed):
      - bugfix: something was broken, now fixed
      - feature: new capability or functionality added
      - refactor: code restructured, behavior unchanged
      - change: generic modification (docs, config, misc)
      - discovery: learning about existing system, reviewing documentation, understanding patterns  ← UPDATE THIS
      - decision: architectural/design choice with rationale
  -->
```

And update the "WHEN TO SKIP" section (line 58):

```typescript
WHEN TO SKIP
------------
Skip routine operations:
- Empty status checks
- Package installations with no errors
- Simple file listings
- Repetitive operations you've already documented
- If file reads produced no usable content  ← CHANGE FROM "file related research"
- **No output necessary if skipping.**
```

**Pros**: Minimal change, clarifies existing observation type
**Cons**: Doesn't explicitly encourage recording context-loading tasks

### Option 2: Add Context-Loading Task Guidance (Better)

Add explicit guidance about research/learning tasks in `buildInitPrompt()`:

```typescript
// Add new section after "WHAT TO RECORD" (around line 50):

CONTEXT-LOADING TASKS
---------------------
When user requests understanding/learning (e.g., "review and understand files"):
- These ARE valuable observations (type: discovery)
- Record what was learned, not that learning occurred
- Focus on insights, patterns, rules discovered
- Even without deliverable code, knowledge gained matters

✅ GOOD EXAMPLES:
- "Project follows TDD workflow with RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle"
- "Continuous improvement rules emphasize trust-but-verify and fix-forward approach"
- "Authentication system uses OAuth2 PKCE flow for security"

❌ BAD EXAMPLES:
- "Read and analyzed rules documentation"
- "Reviewed continuous improvement files"
```

**Pros**: Clear guidance, encourages proper recording
**Cons**: Longer prompt, adds tokens

### Option 3: Separate Summary Logic for Non-Deliverable Tasks (Best)

Update summary generation to detect context-loading vs action-oriented tasks:

```typescript
// In buildSummaryPrompt(), add guidance:

When summarizing:
1. If Read tool succeeded → files WERE found (do not report as missing)
2. Context-loading tasks (review/understand/learn) are complete when files are read
3. No deliverable artifact ≠ no work completed
4. Record insights gained, even if no code was written
```

**Pros**: Addresses root cause directly
**Cons**: Still relies on LLM interpretation

## Workaround

**Current workarounds:**

1. **Rephrase requests** as action-oriented tasks with deliverables:
   - ❌ "Review and understand rules.md"
   - ✅ "Create a summary document of rules.md findings"

2. **Accept inaccurate summaries** for pure context-loading tasks and rely on observation records instead

3. **Manual verification**: Check that Read tool succeeded regardless of what summary reports

## Additional Context

Context-loading is a fundamental development workflow. Developers frequently need to:
- Review existing code/docs to understand systems
- Load project context before making changes
- Study patterns and best practices
- Understand dependencies and architecture

These research activities are valuable and should be recorded in the memory system. Currently, the SDK agent's deliverable-focused framing causes it to skip or misreport these legitimate activities, making memory search less useful for understanding what knowledge has been gathered over time.

The `discovery` observation type exists precisely for this use case, but the system prompt's emphasis on deliverables and instruction to skip "file related research" prevents it from being used correctly.

---

Thank you for claude-mem! It's a fantastic tool and this fix would make observations more comprehensive. Happy to provide any additional details or testing.

title: Vertex AI - gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview intergration
body:
Hi, while using the vertex platform, i want to use the gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview.

So i add it to the catalog, add the different capabilities, (set up the google cloud adc..).

When i want to fetch the result, the only way for me to get the image binary is to use the getRawResult method of the reponse.

In fact in Bridge/VertexAi/Gemini/ResultConverter.php::128 (convertChoice) cannot handle inline_data response as content part and cant return BinaryResult.

I managed to make it work easily adding the case 

```php
if (isset($contentPart['inlineData'])) {
    return new BinaryResult($contentPart['inlineData']['data'], $contentPart['inlineData']['mimeType'] ?? null);
}
```
and adding BinaryResult as function return type.


See you, thanks for the work

title: Feature Request: Configurable Network Access Control for Codex Sessions
body:
# Feature Request: Configurable Network Access Control for Codex Sessions ## Problem Statement Currently, Codex sessions in Agor run with `network_access` set to `restricted` mode, which blocks external HTTP requests including web searches and API calls. This limitation prevents agents from: - Fetching external documentation (e.g., SDK changelogs, API references) - Performing web searches to answer current questions - Accessing third-party APIs during development tasks - Retrieving up-to-date information beyond their knowledge cutoff **Example user impact:** When asked to research the Codex SDK changelog, the agent responds: _"I'm not allowed to ask for an exception in this mode. If you can share the changelog text, I'll work from that."_ This creates friction in workflows where agents need external information, forcing users to manually gather and paste content. ## Proposed Solution Add configurable network access controls to Codex sessions with two integration points: ### 1. Session Settings (Persistent Configuration) ### 2. Conversation Footer Quick-Toggle (In-Session Control) --- ## Detailed Design ### Network Access Modes Implement three security levels aligned with Codex SDK capabilities: | Mode | SDK Setting | Behavior | Security Level | |------|-------------|----------|----------------| | **Disabled** (default) | `network_access = false` | No external network requests | 🔒 Most secure | | **Web Search Only** | `--search` flag | Built-in web search tool only, no arbitrary URLs | 🔍 Recommended | | **Full Network Access** | `network_access = true` | Unrestricted outbound HTTP/HTTPS | ⚠️ Requires caution | ### Implementation Architecture #### 1. Type System Updates **File:** `packages/core/src/types/agentic-tool.ts` ```typescript export type NetworkAccessMode = 'disabled' | 'search-only' | 'enabled'; export interface CodexPermissionConfig { sandboxMode?: CodexSandboxMode; approvalPolicy?: CodexApprovalPolicy; networkAccess?: NetworkAccessMode; // NEW } ``` #### 2. Codex SDK Integration **File:** `packages/core/src/tools/codex/prompt-service.ts` Modify `writeCodexConfig()` method (currently lines 149-254): ```typescript private async writeCodexConfig( sessionDir: string, approvalPolicy: CodexApprovalPolicy, networkAccess: NetworkAccessMode = 'disabled' // NEW parameter ): Promise { const config = ` [sandbox_workspace_write] network_access = ${networkAccess === 'enabled'} `; // Write to ~/.codex/config.toml } // Update preparePrompt() to pass --search flag when needed (lines 370-384) private async preparePrompt( prompt: string, sessionConfig: Session ): Promise { const networkMode = sessionConfig.permission_config?.codex?.networkAccess; const searchFlag = networkMode === 'search-only' ? '--search' : ''; // ... } ``` #### 3. Session Settings UI **File:** `apps/agor-ui/src/components/SessionSettingsModal/SessionSettingsModal.tsx` Add to Codex configuration section (after sandbox/approval selectors): ```tsx {agenticTool === 'codex' && (
🔒 Disabled No external requests (default, most secure) 🔍 Web Search Only Built-in search tool, no arbitrary URLs (recommended) 🌐 Full Network Access ⚠️ Unrestricted outbound access (caution: prompt injection risk)
)} ``` #### 4. Conversation Footer Quick-Toggle (NEW Component) **File:** `apps/agor-ui/src/components/ConversationFooter/NetworkAccessToggle.tsx` Create a new clickable badge/icon that cycles through modes: ```tsx interface NetworkAccessToggleProps { sessionId: string; currentMode: NetworkAccessMode; onModeChange: (mode: NetworkAccessMode) => Promise; } export function NetworkAccessToggle({ sessionId, currentMode, onModeChange }: Props) { const MODES: NetworkAccessMode[] = ['disabled', 'search-only', 'enabled']; const cycleMode = async () => { const currentIndex = MODES.indexOf(currentMode); const nextMode = MODES[(currentIndex + 1) % MODES.length]; await onModeChange(nextMode); }; const icon = { 'disabled': '🌐🚫', 'search-only': '🔍', 'enabled': '🌐✓' }[currentMode]; return ( {currentMode} ); } ``` **Integration point:** Add to existing conversation footer alongside sandbox/approval indicators (similar to how PermissionModeSelector displays dual badges). **Behavior:** - Click to cycle: `disabled` → `search-only` → `enabled` → `disabled` - Auto-saves to session via PATCH `/sessions/:id` API - Shows loading state during save - Displays warning color when `enabled` mode is active #### 5. Database & Persistence **Storage:** Uses existing `sessions.data` JSON blob column (no migration required) ```json { "permission_config": { "codex": { "sandboxMode": "workspace-write", "approvalPolicy": "on-request", "networkAccess": "search-only" // NEW field } } } ``` **API Endpoint:** Existing `PATCH /sessions/:id` (SessionsService in Feathers pattern) **Repository:** `packages/core/src/db/repositories/sessions.ts` - SessionRepository.update() already handles permission_config merging (lines 305-366) --- ## User Experience Flow ### Initial Setup (Session Settings) 1. User creates/edits a Codex session 2. Sees "Network Access" section with three radio options 3. Selects desired mode (defaults to "Disabled") 4. Reads security warning for "Full Network Access" 5. Clicks "Save Settings" → persisted to database ### In-Conversation Quick Toggle 1. User starts conversation with network disabled 2. Agent says "I cannot access external URLs" 3. User clicks network badge in footer: `🌐🚫 disabled` 4. Badge cycles to `🔍 search-only` 5. User sends next message 6. Agent now has web search capability 7. User clicks again → `🌐✓ enabled` (warning color) 8. Agent now has full network access ### Mid-Session Reconfiguration Similar to existing approval policy changes (detected in CodexPromptService lines 416-460): - Detects network mode change - Rewrites `~/.codex/config.toml` - Sends in-band message: `/network enabled` or equivalent - No session restart required --- ## Security Considerations ### Default-Deny Posture - All new sessions default to `disabled` - Existing sessions without explicit config → `disabled` - Upgrade path preserves security (no automatic enablement) ### User Warnings - Prominent ⚠️ icon next to "Full Network Access" option - Warning text: _"Enabling full network access may expose the agent to prompt injection attacks where malicious websites trick the agent into executing unintended commands."_ - Visual indicator (red/orange badge) when enabled in footer ### Audit Trail - Network mode changes logged to session history - MCP routes include permission_config in session metadata - Users can review historical network access grants ### Alignment with Codex Best Practices Per Codex security documentation: - Defaults match Codex SDK defaults (network disabled) - "Web Search Only" mode uses `--search` flag (OpenAI-recommended safer alternative) - Full access requires explicit user action --- ## Implementation Checklist ### Backend (packages/core) - [ ] Add `NetworkAccessMode` type to `types/agentic-tool.ts` - [ ] Extend `CodexPermissionConfig` interface - [ ] Update `CodexPromptService.writeCodexConfig()` to write network_access setting - [ ] Add `--search` flag handling in prompt preparation - [ ] Implement mid-session network mode change detection (similar to approval policy) - [ ] Update session repository tests for new permission field ### Frontend (apps/agor-ui) - [ ] Create `NetworkAccessToggle.tsx` component - [ ] Add network access section to `SessionSettingsModal` - [ ] Integrate toggle into conversation footer - [ ] Add security warning UI components - [ ] Implement API call to update session on toggle - [ ] Add loading/error states for toggle clicks ### API Layer (apps/agor-daemon) - [ ] Verify `PATCH /sessions/:id` handles network_access in permission_config - [ ] Update MCP session routes to expose network settings - [ ] Add validation for network mode values ### Documentation - [ ] Update session configuration docs - [ ] Add security guidelines for network access - [ ] Document quick-toggle usage - [ ] Add troubleshooting guide for network issues ### Testing - [ ] Unit tests for network config generation - [ ] Integration tests for session PATCH with network settings - [ ] E2E tests for toggle cycling behavior - [ ] Verify `--search` flag passed correctly to Codex SDK - [ ] Test mid-session network mode changes - [ ] Verify default values for new/existing sessions --- ## Alternative Approaches Considered ### 1. URL Whitelist/Blacklist **Rejected:** Codex SDK only supports binary on/off for network_access. Implementing our own HTTP proxy would add significant complexity and maintenance burden. ### 2. Always-On Network with Permission Prompts **Rejected:** Every HTTP request triggering approval would create poor UX. Codex doesn't provide per-request hooks. ### 3. Environment Variable Override **Rejected:** Less discoverable than UI controls. Doesn't solve mid-session reconfiguration need. --- ## Success Metrics ### Quantitative - % of Codex sessions using "Web Search Only" mode - Reduction in "cannot access external URLs" error messages - Time saved on manual content gathering tasks ### Qualitative - User feedback on quick-toggle convenience - Agent effectiveness at research tasks with search enabled - Support ticket volume related to network restrictions --- ## References ### Codex SDK Documentation - **Security Guide:** https://developers.openai.com/codex/security/ - **Configuration:** https://developers.openai.com/codex/local-config/ - **Sandbox Settings:** `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access` boolean ### Agor Codebase (Current Implementation) - **Permission Types:** `packages/core/src/types/agentic-tool.ts:56-81` - **Codex Config Writer:** `packages/core/src/tools/codex/prompt-service.ts:149-254` - **Session Repository:** `packages/core/src/db/repositories/sessions.ts:305-366` - **Permission Selector UI:** `apps/agor-ui/src/components/PermissionModeSelector/` - **Session Settings Modal:** `apps/agor-ui/src/components/SessionSettingsModal/` --- ## Questions for Discussion 1. **Default for new users:** Should we recommend "Web Search Only" instead of "Disabled" for better out-of-box experience? 2. **Enterprise controls:** Do we need organization-level policies to enforce maximum network access level? 3. **Network usage telemetry:** Should we track/display network requests made by agents (similar to token usage)? 4. **Offline mode indicator:** Should we show network status in real-time (detecting actual connectivity vs permission)? --- ## Related Issues - Link to any existing issues about network restrictions - Link to feature requests for web search - Link to security discussions about agent permissions --- ## Estimated Effort - **Backend implementation:** 2-3 days (Codex config, session updates, mid-session changes) - **Frontend UI:** 2-3 days (toggle component, modal updates, state management) - **Testing & QA:** 1-2 days (unit, integration, E2E tests) - **Documentation:** 1 day (user guides, security warnings, API docs) **Total:** ~1.5 weeks for complete implementation --- **Priority:** High **Labels:** `feature`, `codex`, `security`, `ux-enhancement` **Milestone:** Q1 2025

title: A --continue option, so we don't need to invent and retype chat ids
body:
### Problem

I don't always know when I want to ask ChatGPT a follow-up question. I only know _after_ it has given a response. And I don't want to keep inventing session names (chat ids), just in case I need them. Also, passing chat ids is a lot of typing.

### Possible solution

I suggest a `--continue / -c` option which allows us to continue from the last query we made.

Here is an example:

```sh
$ sgpt 'Ask a question?'
[response]
# I am happy with the answer, and happy for the chat session to end.

$ sgpt 'Ask a different question?'
[response]
# I am not satisfied. I want to continue the discussion with a followup query. So I use -c.
$ sgpt -c 'Ask followup to the previous question?'
[response]
$ sgpt -c 'Ask another followup in the same session?'
[response]
```

Advantage: No session names, and less typing.

### Possible implementation

- Every basic query should start a new chat session, with a randomly generated id.
- `sgpt` could store the id of the latest session somewhere.
- If `--continue` is passed, then instead of starting a new chat session, `sgpt` should continue the latest stored session.

**Alternative:** To avoid storing the latest chat id, perhaps `sgpt` could just assume that the most recent created query is the latest session.

**Alternative:** It might make sense to use `--followup / -f` or `--reply / -r` instead, to keep `-c` as a shortcut for `--chat`

Does this sound like a good idea? Or is there already a good way to do this in `sgpt`?

title: Feature Request: Return session state in List Sessions API in `adk api_server`
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I’m building a chat-UI application using the `adk api_server` List Sessions endpoint (`GET /apps/{app_name}/users/{user_id}/sessions`). I need to display each session’s state or metadata (e.g. an auto-generated title) in a sidebar so users can quickly see past conversations. However, while the single-session endpoint (`GET /apps/{app_name}/users/{user_id}/sessions/{session_id}`) correctly returns the `state` field, the List Sessions API always returns `state` as empty—making it impossible to show any session metadata in the list.

**Describe the solution you’d like**
Modify the List Sessions API to include the `state` field for each session in its response, just as the single-session endpoint does. That way, any metadata stored in `state` (such as a short summary or title generated by a small, fast model) will be available directly in the list response.

**Describe alternatives you’ve considered**

* Fetching every session individually using `GET /apps/{app_name}/users/{user_id}/sessions/{session_id}`, which adds extra HTTP requests and latency.
* Storing session metadata in a separate external database and managing synchronization manually, which complicates the overall architecture.

**Additional context**
The current implementations explicitly clear or omit the `state` field when listing sessions:

* **Database Sessions**:
  [https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/3b5232c14f48e1d5b170f3698d91639b079722c8/src/google/adk/sessions/database\_session\_service.py#L437-L457](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/3b5232c14f48e1d5b170f3698d91639b079722c8/src/google/adk/sessions/database_session_service.py#L437-L457)
* **In-Memory Sessions**:
  [https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/3b5232c14f48e1d5b170f3698d91639b079722c8/src/google/adk/sessions/in\_memory\_session\_service.py#L207-L222](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/3b5232c14f48e1d5b170f3698d91639b079722c8/src/google/adk/sessions/in_memory_session_service.py#L207-L222)

Including `state` in the List Sessions response would enable native support for recording and displaying session metadata without extra workarounds.

title: [MCP Bundle] Add options for tool discovery
body:
The container configuration currently hard codes the directory to be scanned for tools:

```php
# vendor/symfony/mcp-bundle/config/services.php
->call('setDiscovery', [param('kernel.project_dir'), ['src']])
```

The MCP SDK although allows setting multiple `scanDirs` and even `excludeDirs`:

```php
# vendor/mcp/sdk/src/Server/Builder.php
    public function setDiscovery(
        string $basePath,
        array $scanDirs = ['.', 'src'],
        array $excludeDirs = [],
        ?CacheInterface $cache = null,
    ): self {}
```

It would be nice to configure those directories via the bundle configuration. Especially if you define your tools in a small subset of all directories.

## Background

I ran into a problem that I ship the `src/DataFixtures` directory into production where the classes inherit from a base Fixture that is not installed when doing a composer install --no-dev for prod. This has never led to any problems but because the MCP SDK is now running a discovery in full `/src` it fails because of the missing base class.
